Not vendored from RmlUi: Lua, Lottie, Debugger, Backends, Samples, Tests.
`RMLUI_CUSTOM_RTTI` does not exist at this revision; RTTI is detected from the compiler (`Platform.h`).

## Local patches

1. `Include/RmlUi/Core/ID.h`: `PropertyId::MaxNumIds` raised from 128 to 255 (maximum for the `uint8_t` `PropertyId`) to make room for the CSS Grid properties.
2. CSS Grid (`display: grid | inline-grid`), ported from Taffy `src/compute/grid` without subgrid:
   - Added `Source/Core/Layout/GridFormattingContext.{h,cpp}`, `GridLayoutTypes.h`, `GridPlacement.cpp`, `GridTrackSizing.cpp`, `Source/Core/GridDefinition.h` and `Source/Core/PropertyParserGrid.{h,cpp}`.
   - `Include/RmlUi/Core/ID.h`: grid property ids (`GridTemplateColumns/Rows/Areas`, `GridAutoColumns/Rows/Flow`, `GridColumnStart/End`, `GridRowStart/End`, `JustifyItems`, `JustifySelf`) and shorthand ids (`GridRow`, `GridColumn`, `GridArea`, `GridTemplate`, `Grid`).
   - `Include/RmlUi/Core/StyleTypes.h`: `Display::Grid/InlineGrid`, `JustifyContent::Stretch/Normal`, `GridAutoFlow`.
   - `Include/RmlUi/Core/ComputedValues.h`: grid accessors, `justify_items()`, `justify_self()`; `justify-content` defaults to `normal`.
   - `Include/RmlUi/Core/{Types.h,Unit.h,Variant.h,Variant.inl,TypeConverter.h}`, `Source/Core/{Variant.cpp,TypeConverter.cpp}`: `GridDefinitionPtr` variant type and `Unit::GRID`.
   - `Include/RmlUi/Core/PropertySpecification.h`, `Source/Core/PropertySpecification.cpp`: grid shorthand types and `SplitOption::PreserveQuotes`.
   - `Include/RmlUi/Core/PropertyDefinition.h`, `Source/Core/PropertyDefinition.cpp`: `SetPreserveQuotes()` for `grid-template-areas`.
   - `Source/Core/StyleSheetSpecification.cpp`: grid parser and properties; `grid`/`inline-grid` display keywords; `start`/`end` aliases for the alignment keywords and `normal` for `align-content`/`justify-content` (for items/self, `normal` is a separate value since entry 5, with `legacy` mapped to it on `justify-items`).
   - `Source/Core/ElementStyle.cpp`, `Source/Core/Element.cpp`: grid properties fetched on demand; grid items render as atomic units.
   - `Source/Core/Layout/{FormattingContext.h,FormattingContext.cpp,BlockFormattingContext.cpp,LayoutDetails.cpp,LayoutBox.h,LayoutPools.cpp,ContainerBox.h,ContainerBox.cpp}`: grid dispatch, `GridContainer` layout box, inline-grid shrink-to-fit.
   - `Source/Core/Layout/FlexFormattingContext.cpp`: `justify-content: normal | stretch` behave as `flex-start`.
   - `Include/RmlUi/Core/Element.h`, `Source/Core/Element.cpp`, `Source/Core/Layout/ContainerBox.{h,cpp}`: absolutely positioned children of a positioned grid container use their grid area as containing block (`ContainerBox::AddAbsoluteElementInArea`).
   - `Source/Core/Layout/GridFormattingContext.cpp`, `Source/Core/Layout/ContainerBox.{h,cpp}`: out-of-flow grid children whose two insets in an axis are both auto are placed in their static-position rectangle (the grid area, or the grid content box when the grid is not their containing block) by `justify-self`/`align-self`, falling back to `justify-items`/`align-items`; `start`, `stretch`, `normal` and `baseline` align to start.
3. `Source/Core/ElementScroll.cpp` (`EnableScrollbar`), `Source/Core/WidgetScroll.cpp` (`FormatElements`): a scrollbar with auto width (vertical) or auto height (horizontal) has zero thickness instead of filling the scroll container, so unstyled `overflow: auto` no longer collapses the content box to zero width. The auto size is then clamped by `min-width`/`max-width` and `min-height`/`max-height` in `LayoutDetails::BuildScrollbarBox` (`Source/Core/Layout/LayoutDetails.{h,cpp}`), shared by both.
4. `calc()`, `min()`, `max()` and `clamp()` for length-percentage values (grammar after Ladybird `Libraries/LibWeb/Rust/src/css/parser/calc_parser.rs`, BSD-2-Clause):
   - Added `Source/Core/CalcExpression.{h,cpp}` (immutable postfix expression, `Resolve`, length resolution, folding, mixing) and `Source/Core/PropertyParserCalc.{h,cpp}` (parser registered as `calc`). Single-unit expressions fold to a plain numeric property at parse time; others are stored as `CalcExpressionPtr` with `Unit::CALC`.
   - `Include/RmlUi/Core/{Unit.h,TypeConverter.h}`: `Unit` has `uint32_t` as underlying type and gains `Unit::CALC`.
   - `Include/RmlUi/Core/{Types.h,Variant.h,Variant.inl,TypeConverter.h}`, `Source/Core/{Variant.cpp,TypeConverter.cpp}`: `CalcExpressionPtr` variant type, compared by value.
   - `Include/RmlUi/Core/StyleTypes.h`: `LengthPercentage(Auto)::Calc` carrying a `CalcExpressionPtr`.
   - `Include/RmlUi/Core/ComputedValues.h`, `Source/Core/ComputedValues.cpp`: widened type bitfields; calc expressions are owned by `ComputedValues::calc_values` and the value field stores their index; `ResolveValueOr` evaluates calc against the percentage base.
   - `Source/Core/ComputeProperty.cpp`: em, rem, vw, vh, dp and physical units are resolved at compute time; expressions without percentages compute to a plain length.
   - `Source/Core/ElementStyle.cpp`: calc properties are dirtied by the units their leaves use.
   - `Source/Core/StyleSheetSpecification.cpp`: signed `calc` parser on margin and inset.
   - `Source/Core/GridDefinition.h`, `Source/Core/PropertyParserGrid.cpp`, `Source/Core/Layout/{GridLayoutTypes.h,GridPlacement.cpp,GridTrackSizing.cpp}`: calc track breadths and gaps (`GridSizingKind::Calc`, percentage-like); grid item sizes, margins and padding resolve calc.
   - `Source/Core/ElementAnimation.cpp`: animations and transitions involving calc interpolate as `calc(a * (1 - t) + b * t)`, falling back to discrete when the expression would exceed the node limit.
   - `Source/Core/{CalcExpression.{h,cpp},PropertyParserCalc.{h,cpp},StyleSheetSpecification.cpp,PropertyParserGrid.cpp}`: math functions on width, height, min/max sizes, padding, row/column gap, flex-basis and grid track breadths use the `calc_non_negative` parser; their expressions carry a non-negative flag, so parse-time folds and `CalcExpression::Resolve` clamp to zero, while margins and insets stay signed. A number directly followed by an identifier character (`10px-`) is rejected as an unknown unit.
5. `aspect-ratio: auto | <ratio> | auto && <ratio>` (CSS Sizing 4), transfer semantics after Taffy `Size::maybe_apply_aspect_ratio` (MIT, `src/geometry.rs`) and CSS Flexbox/Grid sizing:
   - Added `Source/Core/PropertyParserAspectRatio.{h,cpp}`: a bare `<number>` is parsed here, `<number> / <number>` through the unchanged `PropertyParserRatio`, which media queries keep using.
   - `Include/RmlUi/Core/ID.h` (`PropertyId::AspectRatio`), `Include/RmlUi/Core/StyleTypes.h` (`Style::AspectRatio`), `Include/RmlUi/Core/ComputedValues.h` (`aspect_ratio()`, fetched on demand), `Source/Core/{StyleSheetSpecification.cpp,ElementStyle.cpp}`: property registration.
   - `Source/Core/Layout/LayoutDetails.{h,cpp}`: ratio helpers, ignoring a specified ratio on internal table boxes (`table-row`, `table-row-group`, `table-column`, `table-column-group`, `table-cell`); `BuildBox` transfers a definite width or height to the auto axis (content box, or border box for `box-sizing: border-box`) clamped by that axis' min/max, `BuildBoxSizeAndMargins` derives an auto height from the resolved width, and a specified ratio overrides the intrinsic ratio of replaced elements.
   - `Source/Core/Layout/FlexFormattingContext.cpp`: flex base size from a stretched definite cross size, min/max transferred between axes, auto hypothetical cross size from the used main size.
   - `Source/Core/Layout/{GridLayoutTypes.h,GridFormattingContext.cpp,GridTrackSizing.cpp}`: grid item known dimensions, minimum contribution, block-axis measurement and final sizing apply the ratio of non-replaced items; a stretched size is clamped by its own min/max before the ratio transfers it (the fork's own order; same result as Taffy, which only clamps afterwards), and the result is clamped by min/max transferred through the ratio (Taffy `GridItem::known_dimensions`). Replaced items keep their `BuildBox` size, which already applies their natural or specified ratio.
   - `Include/RmlUi/Core/StyleTypes.h` (`AlignItems::Normal`, `AlignSelf::Normal`), `Include/RmlUi/Core/ComputedValues.h`, `Source/Core/StyleSheetSpecification.cpp`: `normal` is its own keyword for `align-items`, `align-self`, `justify-items` and `justify-self`, and `align-items` defaults to `normal`. Flex (`Source/Core/Layout/FlexFormattingContext.cpp`) treats it as `stretch`. Grid (`Source/Core/Layout/{GridFormattingContext.cpp,GridTrackSizing.cpp}`) treats it as `stretch`, except as `start` in the block axis for items with a ratio and in both axes for replaced items (Taffy `compute/grid/alignment.rs`); an explicit `stretch` stretches a ratio item to its grid area.
6. `text-shadow: none | [ <color>? && <length>{2,3} ]#` (offset-x, offset-y, optional blur; colour defaults to `currentcolor`; first shadow on top), semantics after Ladybird `ShadowStyleValue.cpp` (BSD-2-Clause):
   - Added `Source/Core/PropertyParserTextShadow.{h,cpp}` (parser registered as `text_shadow`); `Include/RmlUi/Core/ID.h` (`PropertyId::TextShadow`), `Source/Core/{StyleSheetSpecification.cpp,ElementStyle.cpp}`: inherited property, fetched with `GetProperty()` and not part of `ComputedValues`. The value reuses `BoxShadowList` / `Unit::BOXSHADOWLIST` (spread and inset stay unused); `Include/RmlUi/Core/DecorationTypes.h` gains `BoxShadow::current_color` (compared by value), `Source/Core/TypeConverter.cpp` prints it as `currentcolor`.
   - `Include/RmlUi/Core/ElementText.h`, `Source/Core/ElementText.cpp`: `UpdateTextShadows` copies the generated text meshes once per shadow with the vertex colour replaced (premultiplied by opacity), rebuilt when the text geometry, `text-shadow`, `font-size`, `color` or `opacity` change. `OnRender` draws the shadow copies translated by the offset before the text, last list entry first. Empty glyph meshes (an invalid `Geometry` from `RenderManager::MakeGeometry`) keep an empty shadow entry so shadow and text geometry stay index-aligned. A blur radius above zero draws that shadow into a pushed layer and composites it with the `blur` filter (sigma = blur radius / 2); a zero radius is a plain offset draw. The visibility test against the scissor region is extended by the largest offset plus 3 sigma.
   - Shadows follow the glyph meshes of all font-effect layers (the shadow of text with `font-effect: outline` is the union of outline and fill); `text-decoration` lines get no shadow. `text-shadow` does not animate or transition (`Source/Core/ElementAnimation.cpp` rejects shadow lists with a warning, as for `box-shadow`; one message shared by both).
   - A blurred shadow is drawn with the scissor region narrowed to its ink rect (the shadow mesh bounds translated by the shadow offset and extended by 3 sigma, projected to window coordinates when the element has a transform, intersected with the current scissor), restored after the layer is composited, and skipped when the rect misses the scissor. `TextShadowLayer::blur_extent` carries the 3 sigma.
7. `rgba()` alpha is a CSS `<number>` in 0-1 or a `<percentage>`, clamped, instead of RmlUi's 0-255 integer (`Source/Core/PropertyParserColour.{h,cpp}`, `ParseRGBColour`); `rgb()` without alpha defaults to 1. Red, green and blue are unchanged (integers 0-255 or percentages). The parser only accepts the comma-separated form, so the slash form `rgb(r g b / a)` is not supported. `hsla()` already read alpha as 0-1 and hex colours are unchanged. Stylesheets written for the old 0-255 alpha (`rgba(0, 0, 0, 128)`) now clamp to opaque.
8. `!important` (CSS Cascade 4: important declarations win over normal ones regardless of specificity; among important ones specificity and order decide):
   - `Include/RmlUi/Core/Property.h`: `Property::important`. `Include/RmlUi/Core/PropertyDictionary.h`, `Source/Core/PropertyDictionary.cpp`: `SetImportantOfAllProperties()`; `Import`/`Merge` keep an important property over a normal one before comparing specificity.
   - `Source/Core/StyleSheetParser.cpp` (`PropertySpecificationParser`): a trailing `!important` (case-insensitive, whitespace allowed after `!`) is stripped and marks every property the declaration expands to; a later normal declaration in the same block no longer overrides an earlier important one. Applies to rules and to the `style` attribute. Inside `@keyframes` blocks a declaration marked `!important` is ignored (CSS Animations 1); `@decorator` blocks do not strip it, so such a declaration fails to parse as upstream.
   - `Source/Core/ElementStyle.{h,cpp}`, `Source/Core/PropertiesIterator.h`: an important rule property beats a normal inline property (plain, custom and var shorthand properties); the local-property iterators skip the overridden inline entry. `UpdateDefinition` treats a change of importance as a change.
   - `Source/Core/Element.cpp`: values written by transitions are important, so transitions run on properties whose target comes from an important rule (CSS: transitions override important declarations); animation values stay normal.
9. CSS-wide keywords `inherit`, `initial` and `unset` for every property and shorthand:
   - `Include/RmlUi/Core/{Unit.h,TypeConverter.h}`: `Unit` has `uint64_t` as underlying type and gains `Unit::INHERIT` and `Unit::INITIAL`; `Source/Core/CalcExpression.cpp` follows the wider type.
   - `Include/RmlUi/Core/PropertyDefinition.h`, `Source/Core/PropertyDefinition.cpp`: `ParseValue` turns the keywords into a property with one of these units (`unset` maps to `inherit` for inherited properties, otherwise `initial`); `ParseCssWideKeyword`. `Source/Core/PropertySpecification.cpp`: a shorthand declared as one keyword sets all its longhands, recursively.
   - `Source/Core/ElementStyle.{h,cpp}`: `inherit` resolves to the parent's specified property and `initial` to the property's default, in `GetSpecifiedProperty`, `GetProperty`, `GetLocalPropertyWithResolvedVariables` and `ComputeValues`. Inherited values are computed with the parent's font size, so `em` lengths keep the parent's computed value; `font-size: inherit` and `line-height: inherit` copy the parent's computed value. A parent's dirty properties are propagated to children that declare them as `inherit` (`GetInheritKeywordProperties`, cached per definition in `Source/Core/ElementDefinition.{h,cpp}`).
   - Known gap: a `var()` that resolves to `inherit` is resolved, but the child is not dirtied when the parent changes.
10. Easing functions and animation parsing (CSS Easing 1, CSS Animations 1):
   - `Include/RmlUi/Core/Tween.h`, `Source/Core/Tween.cpp`: `Tween::CubicBezier` (`Tween(x1, y1, x2, y2)`, Newton iteration with bisection fallback) and `Tween::Steps` (`Tween(num_steps, StepPosition)` with `jump-start | jump-end | jump-none | jump-both`); `reverse()`, comparison and `to_string()` cover both.
   - `Source/Core/PropertyParserAnimation.cpp`: keywords `ease`, `ease-in`, `ease-out`, `ease-in-out`, `linear`, `step-start`, `step-end`, functions `cubic-bezier()` and `steps()` (`start`/`end` aliases), fill modes `none | forwards | backwards | both`, directions `normal | reverse | alternate | alternate-reverse`, play states `running | paused`, and times in `s` or `ms`. RmlUi's own tween names (`quadratic-in-out`, ...) keep working. Lists are split on commas outside brackets and arguments on whitespace outside brackets. Only one identifier may be the keyframes name (a second one invalidates the declaration); the first `none` is the fill mode, an animation without a name is dropped. In transitions, an unknown property name drops only that transition, `allow-discrete` is ignored, and a transition without a property name applies to `all`.
   - `Include/RmlUi/Core/Animation.h`: `AnimationFillMode`, `Animation::fill_mode` and `Animation::reverse`. `Source/Core/ElementAnimation.{h,cpp}`: `SetPlayback`; backwards fill applies the first value during the delay; the first update after the start time is not clamped to 0.1 s, so negative delays start the animation part-way. Completed iterations are advanced arithmetically (`floor(elapsed / duration)`, capped by the iteration count, keeping the alternate-direction parity and the fractional remainder), and an animation with a duration of zero or less completes on its first update. `Source/Core/Element.cpp`: forwards-filling animations stay in the animation list holding their end value after `animationend`, and are removed when the `animation` property changes. The end value is set once, by the final update, and stays applied; a held animation sets no property afterwards (`UpdateAndGetProperty` returns an empty property once complete).
11. `color-mix(in srgb, <color> <percentage>?, <color> <percentage>?)` (CSS Color 5) in `Source/Core/PropertyParserColour.{h,cpp}` (`ParseColorMix`): percentages in either order, a missing one is the complement of the other, both missing are 50% each; when the sum differs from 100% they are normalized and a sum below 100% scales the result's alpha. Mixing is done on premultiplied sRGB, so `transparent` operands only fade the other colour. Operands are any colour the parser accepts, including nested `color-mix()`; `var()` is substituted before parsing. Only the `srgb` interpolation space is accepted.
12. `border-radius` length-percentage: `Source/Core/StyleSheetSpecification.cpp` registers the four corner radii with `length_percent` and `calc_non_negative`; `Include/RmlUi/Core/ComputedValues.h`, `Source/Core/ComputedValues.cpp` store them as `LengthPercentage` and resolve them with `border_radius(border_box_size)` (`has_border_radius()` for the clip test in `Source/Core/ElementUtilities.cpp`); `Source/Core/ElementStyle.cpp` computes them, `Source/Core/Element.cpp` (`GetRenderBox`) and `Source/Core/BoxShadowCache.cpp` pass the border box. Corners stay circular: a percentage resolves against the smaller side of the border box, which matches CSS for square boxes; non-square boxes get a stadium instead of CSS's elliptical corners.
13. `line-height: normal`, the new default (was `1.2`): `Include/RmlUi/Core/StyleTypes.h` (`LineHeight::Normal`, `NormalFallbackFactor`), `Include/RmlUi/Core/ComputedValues.h` (2-bit inherit type), `Source/Core/ComputeProperty.cpp`, `Source/Core/StyleSheetSpecification.cpp`. `Source/Core/ElementStyle.cpp` resolves it after the font face handle to the font's line spacing (`FontMetrics::line_spacing`, FreeType `size->metrics.height`: ascent + descent + line gap), or 1.2 times the font size without a font face; it is inherited as `normal` and recomputed with each element's own font.
14. `calc()`, `min()`, `max()` and `clamp()` in transform function arguments: `Source/Core/PropertyParserTransform.{h,cpp}` reads arguments up to the next comma or parenthesis outside brackets and parses math functions with `PropertyParserCalc::ParseMathFunction` over the argument's units (numbers for `scale*`/`matrix*`, angles for `rotate*`/`skew*`, lengths and percentages for `translate*`). Single-unit results fold to a plain argument. A translation over several units is split by `LinearizeCalcExpression` (`Source/Core/CalcExpression.{h,cpp}`) into one translation per unit, so `translate(calc(-50% + 10px), -20px)` becomes `translate(-50%, -20px) translate(10px, 0px)` and percentages keep resolving against the border box; `min()`/`max()`/`clamp()` over different units are rejected there. `Source/Core/PropertyParserCalc.{h,cpp}`: `deg`/`rad` units and unitless results when the allowed units are only `NUMBER`; `FoldCalcExpression` folds unitless expressions.
15. Property aliases: `Include/RmlUi/Core/PropertySpecification.h`, `Source/Core/PropertySpecification.cpp` (`RegisterAlias`): declarations of an alias are forwarded to the target property or shorthand, with optional keyword replacement per comma-separated item; an empty or not (yet) registered target accepts and ignores the declaration. `Source/Core/StyleSheetSpecification.cpp` registers `-webkit-backdrop-filter` → `backdrop-filter`, `-webkit-mask` → `mask`, `-webkit-mask-composite` → `mask-composite` (`source-over` → `add`, `source-out` → `subtract`, `source-in` → `intersect`, `xor` → `exclude`), and ignores `text-wrap` and `user-select`. The `-webkit-mask` aliases take effect with entry 23, which also adds `-webkit-mask-image` → `mask-image`.
16. `font-family` lists: `Source/Core/StyleSheetSpecification.cpp` keeps the quotes of the declared value; `Source/Core/FontEngineDefault/FontProvider.cpp` (`GetFontFaceHandle`) splits the comma list outside quotes; a quoted name is a literal family name with its exact inner text (so `"serif"` names a family called serif, not the generic), an unquoted name has its whitespace collapsed. It returns the first family that has loaded faces, and maps the unquoted generic family keywords (`serif`, `sans-serif`, `monospace`, `cursive`, `fantasy`, `system-ui`, `ui-*`, `math`, `emoji`, `fangsong`) to the first fallback face, skipping them when none is loaded.
17. `border-style` (CSS Backgrounds 3) with `none | hidden | solid | dashed | dotted` (`hidden` behaves as `none`):
   - `Include/RmlUi/Core/ID.h` (`PropertyId::Border{Top,Right,Bottom,Left}Style`, `ShorthandId::BorderStyle`), `Include/RmlUi/Core/StyleTypes.h` (`Style::BorderStyle`), `Include/RmlUi/Core/ComputedValues.h` (rare values), `Source/Core/{StyleSheetSpecification.cpp,ElementStyle.cpp,Element.cpp}`: the initial value is `none` as in CSS (upstream RmlUi has no border style, so a border width alone used to draw); a side whose style is `none` computes its border width to 0, which also removes it from layout. Stylesheets must now declare a style, e.g. `border: 1px solid <color>`.
   - `Include/RmlUi/Core/PropertySpecification.h`, `Source/Core/PropertySpecification.cpp`: new `ShorthandType::AnyOrder` (values in any order, each assigned to the first unset longhand that parses it, omitted longhands reset to their defaults); `border-top/right/bottom/left` (and through them `border`) use it with width, style and color.
   - `Include/RmlUi/Core/RenderBox.h`: `RenderBox::{Get,Set}BorderStyles` (solid unless set; compared in `operator==`), filled by `Element::GetRenderBox`.
   - `Source/Core/{GeometryBackgroundBorder.{h,cpp},MeshUtilities.cpp}`: `DrawPatternedBorder` draws dashed and dotted sides (centerline construction after Ladybird `Libraries/LibWeb/Rust/src/painting/record/paint/border.rs`, BSD-2-Clause; proportions and pattern fitting replaced by the Chromium port of entry 26).
18. `background` / `background-image` image layers (CSS Backgrounds 3) written to the `decorator` longhand, so there is one computed source and `transition: background` maps to `decorator` and `background-color`:
   - `Source/Core/StyleSheetSpecification.cpp`: `background` is a shorthand of `decorator, background-color`, `background-image` of `decorator`, both `ShorthandType::BackgroundLayers` (`Source/Core/PropertySpecification.cpp`, `ParseBackgroundLayersShorthand`): layers are split on commas outside brackets, the last layer may hold a colour, `none` layers are dropped, and a `background` without colour or image resets the other longhand to its default (`background: red` clears an earlier decorator, as in CSS).
   - `Include/RmlUi/Core/DecorationTypes.h` (`DecoratorLayer`: position, size `auto | cover | contain | <length-percentage>{1,2}`, repeat per axis, positioning box), `Include/RmlUi/Core/StyleSheetTypes.h` (`DecoratorDeclaration::layer`), `Source/Core/PropertyParserDecorator.{h,cpp}`: decorator items accept `<position> [/ <size>]?`, `repeat | no-repeat | repeat-x | repeat-y | space | round` (one or two values; `space` and `round` act as `repeat`), and `scroll | fixed | local` (ignored), in any order (box keywords moved to `background-origin` / `background-clip`, entry 24), for `linear-`, `radial-` and `conic-gradient` and their repeating forms; other decorator types keep upstream syntax. Positions take one or two values (keywords or length-percentage); the three- and four-value offset forms are rejected.
   - `url(<path>)` layers become the `image` decorator: `cover`/`contain` map to its fit modes, `auto` size to `repeat`, `repeat-x`, `repeat-y` or `scale-none`, `100% 100%` to `fill`, and the position to its alignment; other explicit sizes are rejected with a warning. Relative paths resolve against the stylesheet and must stay inside the document roots.
   - `Include/RmlUi/Core/Decorator.h`, `Source/Core/Decorator.cpp`: `Decorator::GenerateLayerElementData(element, paint_area, layer)`, defaulting to `GenerateElementData`; `Source/Core/ElementEffects.{h,cpp}` pass the declaration's layer. `Source/Core/DecoratorGradient.{h,cpp}`: the gradient decorators size their shape to the tile and clip the paint-area mesh (with its rounded corners) to each tile (Sutherland-Hodgman), texture coordinates relative to the tile; at most 256 tiles per axis. A default layer generates the upstream geometry.
   - `Source/Core/ElementAnimation.cpp`: decorators interpolate only when their layers are equal (and, as upstream, type and property count match; colour stop lists of equal length interpolate); otherwise the change is discrete.
   - Known limits: there are no separate `background-position`, `background-size` or `background-repeat` longhands.
19. `-webkit-text-stroke: <width> || <color>` (`-webkit-text-stroke-width`, `-webkit-text-stroke-color` defaulting to `currentcolor`; inherited, fetched with `GetProperty()`): `Include/RmlUi/Core/ID.h`, `Source/Core/{StyleSheetSpecification.cpp,ElementStyle.cpp}`. `Source/Core/ElementText.cpp` (`UpdateFontEffects`) inserts an outline font effect of half the stroke width behind the fill, after the other back-layer effects; the effects are cached per width and colour (cleared at 256 entries). `paint-order` is accepted and ignored (`RegisterAlias("paint-order", "")`): the stroke is always behind the fill, so the inner half of a `paint-order: normal` stroke is not drawn. `Source/Core/FontEffectOutline.{h,cpp}`: the outline width is a float with a kernel radius of its ceiling, so `0.5px` gives a partial-coverage 1px ring; fractional `font-effect: outline()` widths are no longer truncated.
20. Generic font families: `Include/RmlUi/Core/Core.h`, `Source/Core/Core.cpp` (`Rml::SetGenericFontFamilies(map, fallback_family)`), `Include/RmlUi/Core/FontEngineInterface.h`, `Source/Core/FontEngineInterface.cpp` (virtual, default no-op), `Source/Core/FontEngineDefault/{FontEngineInterfaceDefault.{h,cpp},FontProvider.{h,cpp}}`. An unquoted family name found in the map resolves to the mapped family when it is loaded; otherwise generic keywords still fall back to the first fallback face. Faces of the configured fallback family are added as fallback faces when loaded, ordered normal style first and by distance from weight 400. A `font-family` value with an unclosed quote keeps its trailing item: the unmatched quote is dropped and the item is a quoted literal (the stylesheet parser already rejects such declarations, so this only affects values set through the API). The map is supplied by `UArcRmlUISettings` (`Config=Game`) through the ArcRmlUI UI thread before fonts load.
21. Anonymous flex and grid items (CSS Flexbox 1 §4, CSS Grid 1 §6): a text node directly inside a flex or grid container is formatted as an anonymous block item. `Source/Core/Layout/BlockFormattingContext.cpp`: formatting a text element independently adds the element itself as the inline content of its block container; `Source/Core/Layout/InlineLevelBox.cpp`: when the text element is its own offset parent, its lines are placed relative to its own origin, which the flex or grid container positions. `Source/Core/Layout/{LayoutDetails.{h,cpp},FlexFormattingContext.cpp,GridFormattingContext.cpp}`: text nodes containing only white space generate no item (their lines are cleared). Known limit: adjacent text nodes form separate items instead of one.
22. `::before` / `::after` pseudo-elements and `content` (CSS Pseudo-Elements 4, CSS Generated Content 3; box construction after Blitz `blitz-dom/src/layout/construct.rs` (MIT) and Ladybird `Libraries/LibWeb/Rust/src/layout/tree_builder.rs` (BSD-2-Clause)):
   - `Include/RmlUi/Core/Types.h` (`PseudoElement`), `Source/Core/StyleSheetSelector.{h,cpp}` (`CompoundSelector::pseudo_element`, specificity of a type selector), `Source/Core/StyleSheetParser.cpp`: `::before`, `::after` and the legacy `:before`, `:after` (case-insensitive) are pseudo-elements instead of never-matching pseudo-classes, also after `*` (`*::before`); a pseudo-class or pseudo-element with an empty name (`a:`, `a::`) makes the selector invalid; a selector with anything after the pseudo-element (including `::before:hover` and further compounds) is invalid. Other `::name` selectors keep upstream behaviour (a pseudo-class that never matches).
   - `Source/Core/StyleSheetNode.{h,cpp}`, `Include/RmlUi/Core/StyleSheet.h`, `Source/Core/StyleSheet.cpp`: a pseudo-element node matches only the generated box of that type, by matching the rest of the selector against the originating element (`IsApplicableToOriginatingElement`); other nodes never match generated boxes, so `querySelector` and `:not()` ignore them. `GetElementDefinition` also reports which pseudo-elements have applicable rules declaring `content` (`ElementStyle::GetPseudoElementRules`).
   - `content: none | normal | [ <string> | attr(<ident>) ]+` (not inherited, initial `normal`, forces layout): `Include/RmlUi/Core/ID.h` (`PropertyId::Content`), `Source/Core/{StyleSheetSpecification.cpp,ElementStyle.cpp}`, added `Source/Core/PropertyParserContent.{h,cpp}` (strings with CSS escapes, `attr()` of the originating element, a missing attribute is empty). `Source/Core/PropertySpecification.cpp`: properties that preserve quotes (`content`, `font-family`, `grid-template-areas`) keep backslash escapes verbatim inside strings for their own parser.
   - `Include/RmlUi/Core/Element.h`, `Source/Core/Element.cpp`: when its definition updates, an element creates a non-DOM child box (`AppendChild(…, false)`, tag `::before`/`::after`, `GetPseudoElementType()`) for each pseudo-element with such rules and removes it when they stop applying; the box inherits from the originating element, runs its own transitions and animations, and holds one text child with the resolved content (re-resolved when an attribute the box reads through `attr()` changes; other attribute changes, including `class`, leave the box's `content` clean). `Source/Core/ElementStyle.cpp`: a box whose `content` computes to `none` or `normal` gets `display: none`, so it is neither laid out, rendered nor hit. Boxes are not DOM children, so `:empty`, `nth-child` and the other structural selectors, `GetNumChildren()`, inner RML and data bindings ignore them.
   - Ordering: `Element::GetNumLayoutChildren()` / `GetLayoutChild()` give `::before`, the DOM children, then `::after`; `Source/Core/Layout/{BlockFormattingContext,FlexFormattingContext,GridFormattingContext}.cpp` lay out through them, and `Element::AddChildrenToStackingContext` stacks in the same order (as regular children, not atomic non-DOM units), followed by the other non-DOM children (scrollbars, widgets).
   - `Source/Core/EventDispatcher.cpp`: an event dispatched on a generated box (`transitionend`, `animationend` of its own transitions and animations) is retargeted to the originating element, with a `pseudoElement` parameter of `::before` or `::after`.
   - `Source/Core/Context.cpp` (`GetElementAtPoint`): a hit on a generated box or its text targets the originating element (events and `:hover` go to it); `pointer-events: none` on the box lets hits pass through.
   - Known limits: boxes of table, table-row and table-row-group elements and of replaced elements are not laid out; `content` supports no counters, quotes, images or `attr()` fallbacks; pseudo-classes after the pseudo-element are rejected; event listeners attached directly to a box (via `GetPseudoElement`) never fire because events retarget to the originating element; scrollbars of a box with `overflow: auto/scroll` are not clickable because hits retarget to the originating element.
23. Mask layers (CSS Masking 1, compositing order after Ladybird `Libraries/LibWeb/Rust/src/painting/record/paint/background.rs`, BSD-2-Clause):
   - `Include/RmlUi/Core/ID.h` (`PropertyId::MaskComposite`, `MaskOrigin`, `MaskClip`, `ShorthandId::Mask`), `Source/Core/StyleSheetSpecification.cpp`: `mask-composite: [add | subtract | intersect | exclude]#` (initial `add`), `mask-origin` and `mask-clip: [border-box | padding-box | content-box]#` (initial `border-box`), all not inherited, stored as the lower-case comma list by the new `keyword_list` parser (`Source/Core/PropertyParserKeywordList.{h,cpp}`). `mask-image` takes the `decorator` parser, which rejects box keywords (entry 24), so the boxes have one source; layers keep the background-layer position, size and repeat syntax of entry 18. `-webkit-mask-image` aliases `mask-image`.
   - `Include/RmlUi/Core/PropertySpecification.h`, `Source/Core/PropertySpecification.cpp`: new `ShorthandType::MaskLayers` (`ParseMaskLayersShorthand`); `mask` splits layers on commas outside brackets and takes from each layer one compositing keyword and up to two box keywords (`<origin> <clip>`, one keyword sets both), writing the rest of the layer to `mask-image`. `mask: none` is accepted alone; a `none` layer inside a list is rejected.
   - `Include/RmlUi/Core/RenderInterface.h`: `BlendMode` gains the Porter-Duff operators `SourceIn`, `SourceOut` and `Xor`, applied by `CompositeLayers` to the whole composite region (inside the scissor and clip mask), also where the source is transparent.
   - `Source/Core/ElementEffects.{h,cpp}`: each mask layer takes its `mask-composite`, `mask-origin` and `mask-clip` value by index, repeating the list when it is shorter than the layer list. Layers are painted bottom-up (the last listed first) into the mask layer; the operator of the bottom-most painted layer is ignored and `add` layers render directly with source-over. Every other layer renders into its own layer and is composited onto the mask with `subtract` → `SourceOut`, `intersect` → `SourceIn`, `exclude` → `Xor`, clipped to the layer's `mask-clip` box (`ElementBackgroundBorder::GetClipGeometry`, with its rounded corners and the element transform) intersected with the element's clip mask, so the mask outside that box is kept, as in Chrome. A layer whose clip box is empty has no effect. `Source/Core/Element.cpp` dirties the effects when the three properties change; `Source/Core/ElementStyle.cpp` lists them as fetched on demand.
   - Known limits: no `mask-mode` (masks use alpha), `mask-position`, `mask-size`, `mask-repeat` longhands, `no-clip`, or SVG geometry boxes; `url()` mask layers are not positioned in their `mask-origin` box (entry 24).
24. Background painting area (CSS Backgrounds 3 §3.7-3.8, §7.2 painting order):
   - `Include/RmlUi/Core/ID.h` (`PropertyId::BackgroundClip`, `BackgroundOrigin`), `Source/Core/StyleSheetSpecification.cpp`: `background-clip: [border-box | padding-box | content-box]#` (initial `border-box`) and `background-origin` (same values, initial `padding-box`), not inherited, `keyword_list` parser, fetched on demand (`Source/Core/ElementStyle.cpp`). `background` is a shorthand of `decorator, background-color, background-origin, background-clip`: `Source/Core/PropertySpecification.cpp` (`ParseBackgroundLayersShorthand`) takes up to two box keywords per layer (one sets both, two set origin then clip; omitted ones reset to the initial values) and writes one list entry per layer; a `none` layer and a final layer without an image become empty decorator layers (`DecoratorDeclaration` with an empty type, parsed from a `none` list item in `Source/Core/PropertyParserDecorator.cpp`, instanced as a null decorator in `Source/Core/StyleSheet.cpp`, interpolated as empty in `Source/Core/ElementAnimation.cpp`, written as `none` by `Source/Core/TypeConverter.cpp`), so the layer indices of `decorator`, `background-origin` and `background-clip` match CSS. `background-image` takes no box keywords.
   - `Source/Core/PropertyParserDecorator.{h,cpp}`, `Include/RmlUi/Core/StyleSheetTypes.h`, `Source/Core/{TypeConverter,ElementAnimation}.cpp`: the decorator parser rejects the box keywords (`border-box`, `padding-box`, `content-box`) for every decorator, including the upstream `<paint-area>` suffix, and `DecoratorDeclaration::paint_area` is removed, so `background-clip` / `background-origin` (and `mask-clip` / `mask-origin`) are the only source of decorator boxes.
   - `Source/Core/ElementEffects.{h,cpp}`: each decorator layer takes its `background-origin` (positioning box) and `background-clip` (paint area) by index, repeating the lists, as mask layers do (`ElementEffectsLayers`, shared with `ElementBackgroundBorder`). Gradient layers tile from the origin box over the clip box, so by default a gradient fills the padding box and repeats under the border, as in Chrome. `Source/Core/Decorator.cpp`: decorators without layer support (`url()` images, `image`, tiled, ninepatch, shader, text, SVG and `@decorator` names) paint the inner of the origin and clip boxes, the padding box by default.
   - `Source/Core/ElementBackgroundBorder.{h,cpp}`, `Source/Core/Element.cpp`: the background colour is a separate mesh clipped to the `background-clip` box of the bottom-most layer (the border box by default, with the outer radii; padding and content boxes use the inner radii), and is rendered first; the decorators follow; the box shadows and the border are rendered last (`RenderBackground` / `RenderBorder`), so translucent borders and the gaps of dashed and dotted borders show the background. `Element.cpp` dirties the background when `background-clip` or `decorator` change and the effects when `background-origin` or `background-clip` change.
   - `Include/RmlUi/Core/MeshUtilities.h`, `Source/Core/MeshUtilities.cpp`: `GenerateBackgroundBorder` is replaced by `GenerateBorder` (border only). `Source/Core/{GeometryBoxShadow.{h,cpp},BoxShadowCache.{h,cpp},BoxShadowHash.h}`: the box-shadow texture holds only the outer and inset shadows (the background and border colours left the cache key), and is drawn above the background layers and below the border, so inset shadows cover gradient backgrounds as in CSS.
   - `Source/Core/GeometryBackgroundBorder.cpp` (`ComputeBorderMetrics`): overlapping radii are scaled against the border box (CSS Backgrounds 3 §5.5) instead of the inner area, so the background, clip and border meshes generated from different boxes share the same outer radii.
   - Known limits: `background-clip: text` is not supported; `url()` layers are not positioned or tiled in the origin box beyond the `image` decorator's fit and alignment.
25. `border-color` initial value `currentcolor` (CSS Backgrounds 3, CSS Color 4): `Source/Core/StyleSheetSpecification.cpp` registers `border-{top,right,bottom,left}-color` with the `currentcolor` keyword (the initial value, also reached through the `border` and `border-*` shorthands) and the colour parser. `Source/Core/ElementStyle.cpp` (`ComputeValues`) resolves each `currentcolor` side to the element's computed `color` after all local properties, and marks the side dirty whenever `color` is dirty, so the border follows inherited, local and transitioned `color` changes. `Source/Core/ElementAnimation.cpp` (`InterpolateProperties`): a `currentcolor` keyword against a colour interpolates through the element's current `color` for any property that parses `currentcolor` as a keyword, so `transition: border-color` from or to the initial value is smooth.
26. Dash and dot proportions match Chromium (ported from `third_party/blink/renderer/platform/graphics/styled_stroke_data.cc` `DashEffectFromStrokeStyle`, `SelectBestDashGap`, `DashLengthRatio`, `DashGapRatio`, `StrokeIsDashed` and `third_party/blink/renderer/core/paint/box_border_painter.cc` `PaintSide`, `DrawCurvedDashedDottedBoxSide`, `DrawLineWithStyle`, `EnforceDotsAtEndpoints`, BSD-3-Clause, `Source/Core/LICENSE-chromium.txt`), in `Source/Core/GeometryBackgroundBorder.cpp` (`DrawPatternedBorder`, namespace `GeometryBackgroundBorderPattern`):
   - Dashes are 3x the width long with 2x gaps below 3px, 2x with 1x gaps from 3px. Dotted sides up to 3px wide are square dots (dashes as long as the width, gaps equal to the width, no gap fitting); on a straight side `EnforceDotsAtEndpoints` adds a start dot and an end dot, each depending on the side length modulo 2, 4 or 6 pixels, growing a dot or moving the first or last gap by one pixel, so both ends are dots as in Chromium; wider dotted sides are round dots of the border width with gaps near the width.
   - Fitting: the gap is chosen by `SelectBestDashGap` (the dash count whose gap deviates least from the nominal gap); a path no longer than two dashes is drawn solid; a path no longer than two dashes and their gaps gets exactly two proportionally scaled dashes; a round-dot path shorter than two dots gets one dot.
   - A side whose inner corners are not rounded is an open path from outer corner to outer corner along the side's centerline, so dashes and dots start and end at the corners; its dashes are rectangles and its dots discs clipped to the side's trapezoid (outer edge, inner edge and the two corner diagonals), so corner pieces of neighbouring sides do not overlap. A side with a rounded inner corner uses one closed centerline of the whole border, starting at the left end of the top side and running clockwise, and draws the pieces of that pattern within its own range (split at the middle of the corner arcs); every such side fits the pattern to the full closed length with its own width and style.
   - Known limits: no anti-aliasing beyond the renderer's; the endpoint adjustments use the side length rounded to whole pixels; other path lengths are not truncated to whole pixels; a dot of a closed path belongs to the side containing its centre instead of being split at the corner diagonal; straight sides of a rounded border whose inner corners are square are not clipped to the outer radius.
27. `drop-shadow()` in CSS argument order (Filter Effects 1, `<color>? && <length>{2,3}`), in `filter` and `backdrop-filter`:
   - `Source/Core/FilterDropShadow.{h,cpp}`: the filter has one property, `shadow`, parsed by the `text_shadow` parser with the `single` parameter (`RecursiveRepeat` shorthand), so the colour may come first or last and defaults to `currentcolor`, resolved from the element's `color` when the filter compiles (a `color` change already recompiles filters through `DirtyEffectsData`). The third length stays the standard deviation, as in Chromium (`third_party/blink/renderer/core/paint/filter_effect_builder.cc`); a missing third length is 0. `drop-shadow(none)`, an empty `drop-shadow()` and a list of shadows are parse errors, so the whole `filter` / `backdrop-filter` declaration is dropped, as in Chrome: the `single` parser rejects `none`, empty values and lists, the `shadow` property has no parsable default, and `Source/Core/PropertyParserFilter.cpp` rejects a filter whose properties still hold an unparsed default after the defaults are applied.
   - `Source/Core/PropertyParserTextShadow.{h,cpp}`: the `single` parameter rejects `none`, empty values and lists; the lengths must be contiguous (`2px red 3px` and `2px red` are rejected), which also applies to `text-shadow`.
   - The `drop-shadow` compile parameter `color` is now a premultiplied `Vector4f`; `ArcRmlUI/Render/ArcRmlRecordingRenderInterface.cpp` no longer premultiplies it.
28. `object-fit: fill | contain | cover | none | scale-down` and `object-position: <position>` (CSS Images 3 §5.5-5.6) for `<img>` and `<svg>`:
   - `Include/RmlUi/Core/ID.h` (`PropertyId::ObjectFit`, `ObjectPositionX`, `ObjectPositionY`, `ShorthandId::ObjectPosition`), `Source/Core/{StyleSheetSpecification.cpp,ElementStyle.cpp}`: `object-fit` (keyword, initial `fill`) and the `object-position` shorthand over the internal longhands `-rmlui-object-position-x` / `-y` (length-percentage or signed `calc()`, initial `50%`), not inherited, fetched on demand.
   - `Include/RmlUi/Core/PropertySpecification.h`, `Source/Core/PropertySpecification.cpp`: new `ShorthandType::Position` (`ParsePositionShorthand`) for the one-, two- and four-value `<position>` forms; keywords map to percentages, keyword pairs may be swapped, and `right` / `bottom` edge offsets become `calc(100% - <offset>)`. The three-value form is rejected, as CSS Values 4 allows it only for `background-position`.
   - `Include/RmlUi/Core/ElementUtilities.h`, `Source/Core/ElementUtilities.cpp` (`GetObjectFitRectangle`): the concrete object size from the natural size and the content box, placed by `object-position` against the remaining space; without a positive natural size the content fills the box.
   - `Source/Core/Elements/ElementImage.cpp`: the quad covers the fitted rectangle clipped to the content box, with texture coordinates cropped to match (replaced content is clipped to its content box, as in Chrome). The natural size is the texture or sprite rectangle times the dp ratio, ignoring the `width` / `height` attributes.
   - `Include/RmlUi/SVG/ElementSVG.h`, `Source/SVG/ElementSVG.cpp`, `Source/SVG/SVGCache.{h,cpp}`, `Source/SVG/DecoratorSVG.cpp`: `SVGCache::GetHandle` takes the render size instead of a box area; `ElementSVG` renders the document at the fitted size and draws its own clipped quad; the natural size is the document's intrinsic size times the dp ratio.
   - Known limits: the fit is not snapped to device pixels; `em` lengths in `object-position` are not re-resolved when only the font size changes. Natural sizes follow the fork's dp-ratio scaling of intrinsic image sizes, so at a dp ratio other than 1 `none` and `scale-down` differ from Chrome at device scale factor 1.
29. Scrollbar styling (CSS Scrollbars 1 and the `::-webkit-scrollbar` pseudo-elements):
   - `Include/RmlUi/Core/ID.h` (`PropertyId::ScrollbarWidth`, `ScrollbarThumbColor`, `ScrollbarTrackColor`, `ShorthandId::ScrollbarColor`), `Source/Core/{StyleSheetSpecification.cpp,ElementStyle.cpp}`: `scrollbar-width: auto | thin | none` (not inherited, forces layout) and `scrollbar-color: auto | <color> <color>` over the inherited internal longhands `-rmlui-scrollbar-thumb-color` / `-track-color`; `ShorthandType::ScrollbarColor` accepts only `auto` or exactly two colours.
   - `Include/RmlUi/Core/Types.h` (`ScrollbarPart`), `Include/RmlUi/Core/Element.h` (`GetScrollbarPart()`), `Source/Core/ElementScroll.cpp`, `Source/Core/WidgetScroll.h` (part accessors): `scrollbarvertical` / `scrollbarhorizontal` are the `Scrollbar` part of their scroll container, `slidertrack` the `Track`, `sliderbar` the `Thumb` and `scrollbarcorner` the `Corner`.
   - `Source/Core/StyleSheetSelector.{h,cpp}`, `Source/Core/StyleSheetParser.cpp`, `Source/Core/StyleSheetNode.{h,cpp}`, `Source/Core/StyleSheet.cpp`: `::-webkit-scrollbar`, `::-webkit-scrollbar-track`, `::-webkit-scrollbar-thumb` and `::-webkit-scrollbar-corner` end a selector like a pseudo-element (also after `*` or alone); pseudo-classes after them (`:hover`) apply to the part element, while other compounds, pseudo-elements or structural selectors after them make the selector invalid. Such a node matches a part element whose scroll container matches the rest of the selector (looked up by the container's id, classes and tag) and never matches through `querySelector` or as an ancestor. Its specificity is that of a pseudo-element plus its pseudo-classes. Other `::name` selectors keep the behaviour of entry 22.
   - Cascade as in Chrome (verified in headless Chrome 154 with both forms on one element): the `::-webkit-scrollbar` rules apply only while the container's `scrollbar-width` and `scrollbar-color` are both `auto` (`ElementScroll::HasNonAutoScrollbarProperties`); `Source/Core/Element.cpp` calls `ElementScroll::UpdateScrollbarStyle` when either changes, which reselects the part rules.
   - With the standard properties in use, `ElementScroll` draws the scrollbar like Chromium's non-overlay Fluent scrollbars through inline properties on the parts (metrics from the Chromium files above): thickness 15px, or 10px for `thin` (2/3, rounded), 0 for `none`; buttons 18px (12px) long with a centred triangle in the thumb colour (a conic-gradient wedge measured against the Segoe Fluent Icons glyph); a thumb of 9px (6px), centred across the track, fully rounded, at least 17px (11px) long; track, buttons and corner in the track colour. Without `scrollbar-color` the light Fluent colours measured in headless Chrome 154 are used (track `#fcfcfc`, thumb and arrows `#8b8b8b`). Switching back to `auto` removes those inline properties.
   - `Source/Core/ElementUtilities.cpp` (`GetClippingRegion`): a scroll container clips its content to the scrollport, the padding box without the scrollbars, so a transparent track shows the container's background as in Chrome; the scrollbars and the corner are unaffected through their `clip: 1`.
   - Known limits: thumb and arrow colours do not change on hover or press in standard mode (Chromium adjusts them by contrast); buttons do not shrink when the scrollbar is shorter than two buttons; the arrow wedge has hard, unantialiased edges; part rules apply even without a matching `::-webkit-scrollbar` rule (Chromium then ignores them and draws the native scrollbar); `::-webkit-scrollbar-button`, `-track-piece`, `-resizer` and pseudo-classes such as `:horizontal` never match; unstyled scroll containers keep the zero-thickness scrollbars of entry 3 instead of Chromium's native 15px scrollbars.
30. `currentcolor` (CSS Color 4) wherever a colour is accepted; keywords are case-insensitive, so `currentColor` works too:
   - `Source/Core/StyleSheetSpecification.cpp`: `color`, `background-color` and `image-color` take the `currentcolor` keyword before the colour parser; `caret-color` and the inherited `-rmlui-scrollbar-thumb-color` / `-track-color` take it next to `auto` (the `scrollbar-color` shorthand accepts it in `Source/Core/PropertySpecification.cpp`).
   - `Source/Core/ComputeProperty.{h,cpp}` (`IsCurrentColorKeyword`): tests a property against its definition's `currentcolor` keyword.
   - `Source/Core/ElementStyle.cpp` (`ComputeValues`): `color: currentcolor` keeps the inherited colour, as `inherit` does; `background-color` and `image-color` resolve to the element's computed `color` after the local properties, like the border sides of entry 25, and are dirtied whenever `color` is. A `color` change also dirties `box-shadow` when one of its shadows uses `currentcolor`, and the scrollbar colours when they are `currentcolor`. `ComputeValue` ignores a keyword for these three properties. `Source/Core/ElementScroll.cpp` resolves `currentcolor` scrollbar colours to the container's `color` and counts them as non-`auto`; `caret-color: currentcolor` falls to the computed `color` in `WidgetTextInput::GenerateCursor` unchanged.
   - `Source/Core/PropertyParserBoxShadow.cpp`, `Source/Core/GeometryBoxShadow.cpp`: `box-shadow` accepts `currentcolor` (`BoxShadow::current_color`), resolved from the element's `color` when the shadow is resolved. An omitted `box-shadow` colour keeps the fork's previous default instead of `currentcolor`.
   - `Include/RmlUi/Core/DecorationTypes.h` (`ColorStop::current_color`), `Source/Core/PropertyParserColorStopList.cpp`, `Source/Core/DecoratorGradient.cpp` (`ResolveColorStops`), `Source/Core/TypeConverter.cpp`: gradient colour stops accept `currentcolor`, resolved when the decorator data is generated (a `color` change regenerates it through `DirtyEffectsData`).
   - `Source/Core/ElementAnimation.cpp` (`InterpolateProperties`): interpolating `color` against `currentcolor` uses the parent's `color`, the value `currentcolor` means for `color` itself.
   - Known limits: `currentcolor` inside `color-mix()` and in `font-effect` colours is not supported.
31. SVG icons follow `color` and take a per-instance `stroke-width`, as an inline `<svg stroke="currentColor">` does in Chrome:
   - `Source/SVG/SVGCache.{h,cpp}`: `GetHandle` takes the element's computed `color` and a `stroke_width`. A document whose source contains `currentColor` and whose root has no `color` attribute renders with the root `color` set to the element's `color`; lunasvg resolves `currentColor` to the inherited `color` (`ThirdParty/lunasvg/source/svglayoutstate.cpp:11,413`). A non-empty `stroke_width` replaces the root's `stroke-width`, which the shapes inherit (`svglayoutstate.cpp:420`); an empty one restores the file's value. Both are applied to the shared document right before each rasterisation (texture callback) and before the crop bounding box. Textures and handles are keyed on the colour (only for documents that use `currentColor`) and the stroke width, next to the existing size, crop and `image-color` keys.
   - `Source/SVG/ElementSVG.cpp`: passes its `stroke-width` attribute, and re-requests the handle when `color` or `stroke-width` changes, so icons follow inherited and transitioned `color` (each new colour rasterises a new texture; the old one is released with its handle). `image-color` still tints the result. `Source/SVG/DecoratorSVG.cpp` passes no stroke width; its colour follows the element's `color`.
32. Zero-duration `animation` and `transition` are valid (CSS Animations 1, CSS Transitions 1): `Source/Core/PropertyParserAnimation.cpp` rejects only negative durations. `Source/Core/ElementStyle.cpp` (`TransitionPropertyChanges`) starts no transition when `max(duration, 0) + delay <= 0`. `Source/Core/ElementAnimation.cpp` (`GetInterpolationFactorAndKeys`): a zero-duration animation picks its key by direction, as in Chrome: during the delay the backwards fill shows the first keyframe of its direction (`to` for `reverse` and `alternate-reverse`), and once complete it yields the opposite one, which `fill-mode: forwards` holds; without forwards fill the property is removed as before. `UI/Rml/Test/CssGroup1Test.rml` has one box per case.
33. `display: contents` (CSS Display 3 §2.5; box-tree hoisting after Blitz `packages/blitz-dom/src/layout/construct.rs` `push_hoisted_child` / `collect_layout_children_with_wrap`, MIT): the element generates no box and its layout children (including its `::before` / `::after`) take its place in the parent's formatting context.
   - `Include/RmlUi/Core/StyleTypes.h` (`Display::Contents`), `Include/RmlUi/Core/ComputedValues.h` (`display` widened to 5 bits), `Source/Core/StyleSheetSpecification.cpp` (`contents` keyword).
   - `Source/Core/Layout/LayoutDetails.{h,cpp}`: `CollectBoxChildren` replaces each `contents` child by its layout children, recursively; `PlaceContentsElement` gives the element an empty box at the origin of the container; `GetBoxParent` skips `contents` ancestors. `Source/Core/Layout/FlexFormattingContext.cpp` and `GridFormattingContext.cpp` collect their items through `CollectBoxChildren`, so the children become flex or grid items of the grandparent (gaps, order, alignment and anonymous text items included). `Source/Core/Layout/BlockFormattingContext.cpp` (`FormatBlockContainerChild`) formats the children in the parent's block container, so block and inline children join the parent's flow. `Source/Core/Layout/FormattingContext.cpp` decides flex/grid itemhood from `GetBoxParent`. The children's offset parent is the container element, so a `contents` ancestor neither offsets nor clips them.
   - `Source/Core/Element.cpp`: `AddToStackingContext` adds the children of a `contents` element in its place with the parent's flex-item status and adds no entry for the element itself, so it paints nothing and is never hit by `Context::GetElementAtPoint`, while its children are painted and hit-tested as children of the parent. A `contents` element never creates a local stacking context (z-index, filters, masks, transforms and perspective on it are ignored for stacking), a `display` change dirties the parent's stacking context, and `UpdateOffset` treats it as statically positioned.
   - `data-if` and `data-for` copy the inline style onto the elements they instance (entry 43), so an inline `style="display: contents"` (or any inline `display`) is kept.
   - Known limits: `contents` inside table internals is not handled by the table layout; `opacity` set on the `contents` element still reaches its descendants, because RmlUi inherits `opacity`; `transform` and `perspective` on it are untested.
   - `UI/Rml/Test/CssGroup1Test.rml` (flex, grid and block parents) and `UI/Rml/Test/MvvmTest.rml` (`data-if` on a `contents` element over a live value) cover it.
34. `Include/RmlUi/Core/Element.h`, `Source/Core/Element.cpp`: `Element::HasRunningAnimations()` returns true while an animation or transition on the element has not completed; completed fill-forwards animations that only hold their end value do not count. ArcRmlUI uses it on the document root to detect the end of an enter/leave transition, since `animationend`/`transitionend` fire once per property.
35. Measurement instrumentation for ArcRmlUI performance logs, compiled only with `RMLUI_ARC_PERF` (defined by `ArcRmlUiCore.Build.cs` for every configuration except Shipping) and recording only while a sink is installed (UI thread only; no sink costs a null check). No behaviour change: no scheduling, caching or rendering decision reads the measurements.
   - Added `Include/RmlUi/Core/ArcPerf.h` (exported API: `SetSink`, bucket/counter/list names, `DescribeElement`, `CollectAnimations`, `GetStyleSheetStats`; `Sink` holds per-call `FrameStats` and per-interval element and name lists), `Source/Core/ArcPerfInternal.h` (scope, counter and timer macros) and `Source/Core/ArcPerf.cpp`. Scopes are timed with `std::chrono::steady_clock` on a stack, so each bucket gets exclusive time and the buckets of a root call (`Context::Update`, `Context::Render`, `Context::LoadDocument`) sum to its total. Element scopes hold an `ObserverPtr`, so elements destroyed during the interval are reported as destroyed.
   - `friend struct ArcPerfAccess` in `Include/RmlUi/Core/{Element.h,StyleSheet.h}` and `Source/Core/{ElementAnimation.h,StyleSheetNode.h}` for reading animations and the stylesheet node index.
   - Scopes and counters in `Source/Core/{Context.cpp,Element.cpp,ElementStyle.cpp,ElementDocument.cpp,ElementText.cpp,ElementEffects.cpp,ElementBackgroundBorder.cpp,ElementScroll.cpp,ElementUtilities.cpp,StyleSheet.cpp,StyleSheetNode.cpp,StyleSheetContainer.cpp,StyleSheetFactory.cpp,DataModel.cpp,DataView.cpp,EventDispatcher.cpp,Factory.cpp,BaseXMLParser.cpp,TemplateCache.cpp,RenderManager.cpp,CallbackTexture.cpp,TextureDatabase.cpp,BoxShadowCache.cpp,GeometryBoxShadow.cpp}`, `Source/Core/Layout/{FormattingContext.cpp,LayoutEngine.cpp}`, `Source/Core/FontEngineDefault/FontFaceLayer.cpp` and `Source/SVG/SVGCache.cpp`. A few single statements gained braces to host a scope (`Context::Update` scroll controller and hover chain, `Element::Render` offsets/stacking context/transform, `FormattingContext::FormatIndependent` cases, `Element::SetClass`, `DataViews::Update`, `ElementScroll::Update`).
36. `Source/Core/Element.cpp` (`Element::Update`): an element requests the next context update only while at least one of its animations is not holding its end value (entry 10), so finished `forwards` animations no longer keep the context updating every frame. With `RMLUI_ARC_PERF`, the update-request attribution lists only those animations.
37. Layout verify mode, a regression harness for layout optimizations (idea after Ladybird's `fc_run_cache` shadow mode), compiled only with `RMLUI_ARC_PERF` and active only while `ArcPerf::SetLayoutVerify` has installed a `LayoutVerifyLog` (ArcRmlUI installs it per view while `ArcRml.LayoutVerify` is 1; otherwise the cost is a null check).
   - `Source/Core/ElementDocument.cpp` (`UpdateLayout`): after the document's layout pass, `ArcPerf::VerifyLayout` captures the result of every element of the document, including non-DOM children (pseudo-elements, scrollbars): main box (content size and all margin, border and padding edges), additional boxes with their offsets, offset parent, relative offset, absolute border offset, baseline, scrollable overflow rectangle, and for text elements the line count, line positions and line text. It then runs the reference layout, a full-document `LayoutEngine::FormatElementReference` against the same containing block, counts the dirty marks it left, captures again and compares field by field with exact float equality (NaN equals NaN); only then are `layout_dirty` and every element's layout dirty state (entry 40) cleared. The reference result is the one left applied, including its `OnResize`/`OnLayout` callbacks and scroll clamping. Only the outermost document layout pass is verified; layout passes nested in a pass, including those run by the reference itself, are not. Each pass record also counts the elements still layout-dirty before the reference (production must leave none; ArcRmlUI logs a non-zero count as a verify failure) and the marks the reference itself left (cleared afterwards). `Context::Update` additionally verifies every document that ran no layout in that update (`ElementDocument::VerifyUnchangedLayout`, the pass record has `layout_ran` false): any mismatch there means a change was not invalidated, and ArcRmlUI reports it as `layout verify missed invalidation`. The reference is always a forced whole-document format that never reads the dirty state or the boundary set. Elements the reference does not format (inside `display: none` subtrees) keep their state through it, so a wrong value there is not reported.
   - `Source/Core/Layout/LayoutEngine.{h,cpp}`: `FormatElementReference` formats like `FormatElement` while `IsReferencePass()` is true, for measurement caches to bypass themselves. Nothing else can set it.
   - `Include/RmlUi/Core/ArcPerf.h`, `Source/Core/ArcPerf.cpp`, `Source/Core/ArcPerfInternal.h`: `LayoutVerifyLog` receives one `LayoutVerifyPass` per verified pass (document source URL, elements compared, mismatched elements, mismatched fields, and the first `max_mismatches` mismatches with the `DescribeElement` descriptor, field, optimized and reference values). The whole verification is timed in the new `layout.verify` bucket with recording suspended (`ArcPerf::SuspendRecording`), so the reference layout adds nothing to the layout buckets, counters or element lists.
38. **Superseded in part by entry 64:** `GetFlexOrGridMaxContentWidth` is deleted (replaced by `GetFlexOrGridFitContentWidth`), the shrink-to-fit clamp is now max(min(min-content, max-content), available), and `GetItemContentWidth` gives flex/grid items the width for its constraint. Original entry: `Source/Core/Layout/LayoutDetails.{h,cpp}` (`GetShrinkToFitWidth`, new `GetFlexOrGridMaxContentWidth`), `Source/Core/Layout/GridFormattingContext.cpp` (`GetItemContentWidth`): the shrink-to-fit width of a non-replaced `flex` / `inline-flex` / `grid` / `inline-grid` element with no definite width comes straight from `FlexFormattingContext::GetMaxContentWidth` / `GridFormattingContext::GetMaxContentWidth`. Upstream first formatted the element under a max-content constraint and then discarded that result, because `FlexContainer` / `GridContainer::GetShrinkToFitWidth` read the formatted box only for a `width` length, which never reaches these paths (a non-negative length makes the built box width definite, so both callers return before formatting). The available-width clamp in `GetShrinkToFitWidth` is unchanged, block containers keep the format-then-measure path, and `FlexContainer` / `GridContainer::GetShrinkToFitWidth` stay for flex and grid boxes inside a measured block container (`BlockContainer::GetShrinkToFitWidth`). The skipped pass also wrote the element's box, scrollbars, absolute children and `OnLayout`; the max-content functions never read them and the final format rewrites them. A negative `width` length (invalid CSS, accepted by the parser) now yields the max-content width instead of the constraint width.
39. Per-pass layout measurement memo (design after RmlUi PR #972, closed unmerged; re-implemented here and extended to grid and table). Added `Source/Core/Layout/LayoutMeasureCache.{h,cpp}`. `LayoutEngine::FormatElement` installs one memo for its pass and restores the enclosing one when it returns, so a nested pass (`ElementUtilities::FormatElement`, used by `WidgetDropDown`) has its own. There is no invalidation: the memo lives for one pass and assumes computed values, text and the DOM do not change during it. Only measurement results are memoized; final formats (`FlexFormattingContext.cpp` item loop, `GridFormattingContext.cpp` item loop, table cell format, absolute elements, block flow) always run, so the last write of every element's box, offset, lines, baseline and scrollbars comes from a final format as before. A memo hit skips the measurement's side effects (intermediate `SetBox`/`OnResize`/`OnLayout`, scrollbar toggles, absolute elements registered with an outer container); each is rewritten by the final format that follows.
   - `LayoutMeasureCache::Lookup` is the only lookup. It runs the computation without the memo outside a pass and while `LayoutEngine::IsReferencePass()` is true, so the layout verify reference never reads or fills it; a hit during the reference pass logs an error and aborts. Keys compare the element pointer, the kind and the exact bit patterns of the float inputs (no tolerance; `-0` and `0` are different keys). ArcPerf counts hits and misses per kind (`measure ... hits/misses`).
   - Keys, derived from the inputs each computation reads:
     - `LayoutDetails::GetShrinkToFitWidth` (split into the memoized wrapper and `ComputeShrinkToFitWidth`): element, containing block (both axes; the box is built from it and the block path formats under a root box of its size).
     - `FlexFormattingContext::GetMaxContentWidth` (`ComputeMaxContentWidth`), `GridFormattingContext::GetMaxContentWidth` (`ComputeMaxContentWidth`): element only. Both format under a fixed 10000 px root box and a container box of zero size, so no outer size or scrollbar state reaches them.
     - `GridFormattingContext::GetItemContentWidth` (`ComputeItemContentWidth`, now static, as it reads no grid state): element, the full item box (content size and all 12 edges), the containing block (the grid area size for grid items), the available-space type and its value.
     - `LayoutMeasureCache::Format`, the format-then-read sites `FlexFormattingContext.cpp` flex base size (column) and hypothetical cross size (row), `GridFormattingContext::MeasureChildSize` and `MeasureChildBaseline`, and both `TableFormattingContext.cpp` cell height formats: element, the containing block `FormatIndependent` resolves from the parent container (`LayoutDetails::GetContainingBlock`, which includes the parent's scrollbars), whether an override box is given, and the full override box. It returns the element's resulting box and last-line baseline. The parent container is otherwise used only as the containing block chain of absolutely positioned descendants, which never feed the measured size (`ContainerBox::ClosePositionedElements` discards their result), and by the shrink-to-fit probe box decision (entry 49), which is always false here: these parents are flex, grid and table containers, never a probe wrapper's block container.
   - Constrained versus unconstrained passes and scrollbar re-runs differ in the override box or containing block, so they get different keys.
40. Per-element layout dirty state (groundwork for partial layout; dirty propagation after the `LayoutNode` of the unmerged upstream branch `partial_layout_update`, ported by hand). Added `Source/Core/Layout/LayoutNode.{h,cpp}`, reached through `ElementMeta::layout_node`. Layout results are unchanged: every document layout is still a full format (until entry 42).
   - `LayoutNode::DirtyLayout` marks the element `Self` dirty and its ancestors `Child` dirty along the real parent chain (pseudo-elements and scrollbar parts included), stopping at the first ancestor that is already marked, or at the nearest layout boundary, which is then added to the owner document's set of boundaries needing a format (`ElementDocument::DirtyLayoutBoundary`, which also sets `layout_dirty`). Boundaries: see entry 42 (`LayoutNode::IsLayoutBoundary`). Elements without an owner document are not marked; attaching a DOM child dirties its new parent, and `Element::SetOwnerDocument` clears the state of an element that changes document, so a marked element always has a marked parent up to its boundary.
   - A `Self` mark records whether the change was box-only. `Element::DirtyLayout()` (all existing callers: DOM insertion and removal, pseudo-elements, text, table spans, images, SVG, form controls) is structural. Only `Element::OnPropertyChange` classifies (`LayoutNode::ClassifyPropertyChange`): box-only when every changed layout-forcing property is `width`, `height`, `min-*`/`max-*`, an inset, `margin-*`, `padding-*`, `border-*-width` or `box-sizing`; the existing absolutely positioned inset case is box-only. Upstream marked only when the document flag was clear (`if (!IsLayoutDirty())`); that gate is removed, so every layout-affecting change is marked per element, and `Element::IsLayoutDirty` / `ElementDocument::IsLayoutDirty`, which had no other caller, are deleted. The `layout dirty calls` counter now counts every such change.
   - `ElementDocument::UpdateLayout` formats through `FormatLayout` (until entry 42, which routes it through `FormatDirtyLayout`), which clears all dirty state and the boundary set (`ClearLayoutDirtyElements`) before `LayoutEngine::FormatElement`. Anything marked during the pass is residual: upstream ignored it. Now the pass logs a warning naming the count and the first `Self`-dirty element, counts `layout residual passes` and `layout residual dirty elements` in ArcPerf, and formats exactly once more; a residual after that pass is logged and cleared. This runs before the layout verify reference (entry 37).
   - `Source/Core/ElementScroll.cpp` (`CreateScrollbar`, `CreateCorner`): the scrollbar parts created during layout compute their properties inside a `LayoutNode::ConsumedDirtyScope`, which drops the marks made while it is alive, because the scroll container formats them afterwards in the same pass. Otherwise every newly shown scrollbar would cause a residual pass. One caller runs outside a document layout: `WidgetTextInput::OnRender` calls `OnLayout` → `FormatElement` when formatting was forced without a layout (value changes); `FormatElement` formats the created scrollbars itself (`ElementScroll::FormatScrollbars`), so the dropped marks are consumed there too, where upstream scheduled one extra document layout.
   - `Source/Core/Context.cpp` (`SetDensityIndependentPixelRatio`): a dp-ratio change marks each document structurally dirty, as `SetDimensions` already does, so the next layout of the document is a full one.
41. Out-of-flow layout inputs stored on the element (groundwork for partial layout; after the margin-origin offsets of the unmerged upstream branch `partial_layout_update`, commits `bd9a212` and `d9064b5`, ported by hand). Layout results are unchanged.
   - `Include/RmlUi/Core/Element.h`, `Source/Core/Element.cpp`, `Source/Core/Layout/ContainerBox.cpp`: `OutOfFlowLayoutInputs` (`Element::out_of_flow_inputs`) replaces the loose grid-area fields of entry 2. `ContainerBox::ClosePositionedElements` writes every input each time it places an absolutely positioned element: the static position at the margin-box origin, relative to the offset parent's border box; the containing block the element is formatted against (`LayoutDetails::GetContainingBlock` of the containing block box, or the grid area); the static-position rectangle and `static_alignment`, which before lived only in the transient `AbsoluteElement`; and the grid-area containing block. `Element::PlaceOutOfFlow` then offsets the element from those inputs and its formatted box: margin edge, then the static alignment of the margin box, then the insets (`UpdateOffset`). An element whose own box changed can therefore be placed again without its containing block.
   - Deviation from upstream: upstream keeps the margin-box origin in `relative_offset_base` (`relative_offset_area`, `SetOffset(..., BoxArea::Margin)`) and subtracts the margin position in every offset reader and in `UpdateRelativeOffsetFromInsetConstraints`. That reorders float additions (`(x - m) + m`, `(s + a) + m`), so offsets would not stay bit-identical. Here the margin-origin static position is the stored input, and `relative_offset_base` stays the border-box offset, computed in the same operation order as before; offset readers are unchanged.
   - `Element::SetOffset`, used by every other placement (flow, flex, grid, table and inline layout, widgets, documents), marks the inputs as not placed, so they are reported only while the element's offset derives from them. The grid-area fields keep their previous lifetime: `UpdateOffset` still reads them after a later `SetOffset`. Since entry 42 the inputs are also marked not placed when the element itself becomes `display: none` or changes owner document (detach); elements inside a hidden subtree keep their last inputs.
   - `ElementDocument::UpdatePosition` is unchanged and consistent with this: it resolves the document's insets at the margin-box origin, adds the margin edge itself and calls `SetOffset`. A document is formatted by `ElementDocument::UpdateLayout`, not placed by a containing block, so it has no stored inputs.
   - `Include/RmlUi/Core/ArcPerf.h`, `Source/Core/ArcPerf.cpp` (with `RMLUI_ARC_PERF`): `ArcPerf::GetOutOfFlowLayoutInputs` returns the inputs of a placed element; `ArcRml.LayoutDump` writes them.
42. Out-of-flow relayout boundaries (partial layout; boundary rule after `LayoutNode::IsLayoutBoundary` of the unmerged upstream branch `partial_layout_update`, ported by hand, with a different propagation rule).
   - `Source/Core/Layout/LayoutNode.{h,cpp}`: a layout boundary is the document, or an element with `position: absolute|fixed` whose display is neither `none` nor `contents` and whose out-of-flow inputs (entry 41) are placed. `Child` marks stop at a boundary as before. A box-only `Self` mark on a boundary marks only the boundary and records it in the document's boundary set; a structural `Self` mark on a boundary (other than the document) propagates to its ancestors like any other element. Upstream always propagates `Self` marks to the parent, so it never isolates an absolute element's own size change. This is exact here because `ContainerBox::ClosePositionedElements` discards the result of formatting an absolutely positioned element: its box never feeds its containing block's size, overflow or scrollbars. Any recorded boundary other than the document can have a clean parent, because `Child` marks stop at it and box-only `Self` marks do not propagate, so `ElementDocument::ClearLayoutDirtyElements` also clears from each recorded boundary. `LayoutNode::CountDirtyRecursive` visits every element.
   - `Source/Core/ElementDocument.cpp`, `Include/RmlUi/Core/ElementDocument.h` (`FormatDirtyLayout`, `CollectOutOfFlowBoundaries`): `UpdateLayout` drops recorded boundaries that were destroyed, belong to another document, lie in a `display: none` subtree (the boundary included) or lie inside another recorded boundary, and formats the remaining ones in isolation. It formats the whole document instead when the document itself is recorded (any structural change that reaches it: load, DOM changes outside boundaries, `SetDimensions`, dp ratio, `display: none` → visible), when nothing is recorded, or when a remaining entry is no longer a boundary. The residual pass after a partial pass is a whole-document format.
   - `Source/Core/Layout/LayoutEngine.{h,cpp}` (`FormatOutOfFlowBoundaries`): under one measurement memo for the pass (entry 39), each boundary is formatted by `FormattingContext::FormatIndependent` under a `RootBox` of its stored containing-block size, the same size `ClosePositionedElements` formats it against (for a grid area, the same `RootBox`). Its own positioning makes it the containing block of every out-of-flow descendant (`LayoutDetails::GetContainingBlock`), so no outer container is read. It is then placed by `Element::PlaceOutOfFlow` against its offset parent, and its subtree gets `ClampScrollOffsetRecursive`. `OnLayout` runs through `SubmitElementLayout` as in a full format.
   - `Source/Core/Element.cpp` (`OnPropertyChange`): an inset change of a placed absolutely or fixed positioned element places it again from its stored inputs (`PlaceOutOfFlow`) instead of `UpdateOffset`, so an inset that returns to `auto` restores the static position without a layout; upstream kept the last offset until the next layout.
   - `Source/Core/ArcPerf.cpp`, `Source/Core/ArcPerfInternal.h`: the verify dirty count (entry 37) also counts the recorded boundaries and the `layout_dirty` flag. ArcPerf counts `layout boundary passes`, `layout boundary formats`, and whole-document fallbacks by reason (`layout full: root dirty`, `layout full: boundary without inputs`); `layout runs` counts whole-document formats.
43. Lazy `data-if` (structural, after `data-for` and Vue `v-if`): a false branch is not instanced.
   - `Source/Core/Factory.cpp`: `if` is registered as a structural data view, so the XML parser stores the element's inner RML as `rmlui-inner-rml` instead of instancing it.
   - `Source/Core/DataViewDefault.{h,cpp}` (`DataViewIf`): the element carrying `data-if` stays as a `display: none` anchor and gets no other data view or controller. The view keeps the anchor's other attributes (all except `data-if` and `rmlui-inner-rml`). When the expression becomes true it instances an element of the anchor's tag with those attributes through `Factory::InstanceElement`, inserts it before the anchor and calls `SetInnerRML` with the stored inner RML (none for a self-closing element, without a warning); when it becomes false it removes that element with `RemoveChild`. The instanced element is held by an `ObserverPtr`, since an enclosing structural view may destroy it first. A branch toggled off and on is rebuilt, so focus, hover, scroll position and state inside it are lost and enter animations replay. The display-toggle path (and with it the saved local `display` of entry 33) is gone.
   - With `data-model` on the same element, the anchor and the instanced element are both attached model roots: the anchor holds the view and is detached by `Context::RemoveDataModel`, and the instanced element is the root of the bound subtree; removing the branch detaches its root.
   - The anchor stays a DOM sibling of the branch, so tree-structural selectors (`:last-child`, `:nth-child`, `:only-child`, `+`, `~`) count it, as they count `data-for` anchors. No ArcRmlUI content uses them on `data-if` elements.
   - `Source/Core/ElementUtilities.cpp` (`ApplyDataViewsControllers`): one structural data view per element. An element with both `data-for` and `data-if` logs an error and keeps `data-for`; the structural view no longer depends on attribute order. `Source/Core/DataViewDefault.cpp` (`DataViewFor`) drops `data-if` from the attributes it copies to rows. `data-if` on an element inside a row works unchanged.
   - `Source/Core/DataView.{h,cpp}` (`DataViews`): views are indexed by element (an intrusive per-element list and their index in the active or pending list), so `OnElementRemove` removes an element's views in constant time instead of scanning every view, and also drops views of the element still waiting to be added.
