Removed views leave the variable map in one batch per update pass (each affected variable's entries are visited once) before the dirty views are collected, instead of a scan of the whole map per removed view. `Update` repeats passes until no views were added and no new variables were dirtied, instead of at most 10 passes, so nested structural views settle within one call; later passes run only the new views, plus the dirty variables' views when new variables were dirtied. After 1000 passes it logs an error and continues on the next update.
   - `Source/Core/Context.cpp` (`Update`, `LoadDocument`), `Source/Core/DataModel.{h,cpp}` and `DataView.h` (`HasPendingViews`): a branch of one model can instance elements bound to another model (GameHUD's resource bars inside a `hud` branch), so after updating every model the context updates each model that still has views waiting, until none has, instead of leaving them to the next context update. After 100 rounds it logs an error and continues on the next update.
   - ArcRmlUI: `ArcRml.LayoutDump` leaves `rmlui-inner-rml` out of the html.
44. Per-frame update of dirty subtrees only (marking after Ladybird `set_needs_layout_tree_update`, `Libraries/LibWeb/DOM/Node.cpp`, and WebKit `childNeedsStyleRecalc`; same shape as `LayoutNode::DirtyLayout`, entry 40). UI-thread only, plain bits.
   - `Include/RmlUi/Core/Element.h`, `Source/Core/Element.cpp`: two bits per element, `needs_update` (self) and `child_needs_update`. `Element::MarkNeedsUpdate()` sets the self bit and the child bit of each ancestor, stopping at the first ancestor whose child bit is already set. Attaching an element (`SetParent`) always marks the new ancestor chain, so a subtree marked while detached is reached once attached.
   - `Element::Update`: the entry stays unconditional (`Context::Update` on the root, `ElementDocument::UpdateDocument`, `ElementScroll::UpdateScrollElementProperties`). The self bit is cleared when the visit starts, so a mark made during the visit (a widget re-arming its timer, an event listener) survives it. The child loop skips a child with neither bit set. The child bit is cleared before the loop and set again from each visited child after its visit; if the children vector shifted during a visit (the visited child removed, or an earlier sibling removed), the child is not read and the bit is rebuilt from all children after the loop, since the shift can skip an unvisited child. After the visit the self bit is set again while the element still has pending update state: a dirty definition or child definitions, dirty properties, variables or var shorthands, a dirty `animation` or `transition` property, or an animation or transition that is not holding its end value (fill-forwards holds do not keep it, entry 36).
   - Writers that mark: `DirtyDefinition` (and the parent for `SelfAndSiblings`), `UpdateDefinition` for each child it dirties, `OnPropertyChange` for `animation` / `transition`, `StartAnimation`, `StartTransition`, `SetParent`. `Source/Core/ElementStyle.{h,cpp}`: `DirtyProperty` (and so `SetProperty`, `RemoveProperty`, `DirtyPropertiesWithUnits*`), `DirtyInheritedProperties`, `SetCustomProperty`, `SetVarShorthand`, `RemoveCustomProperty`, `RemoveVarShorthand`, and the child writes in `ComputeValues` (inherited properties and variables; `inherit` keyword properties only when non-empty). `ElementStyle::UpdateDefinition` writes its dirty sets directly and `Element::UpdateDefinition` sets its own `dirty_child_definitions` without a mark, because both are consumed later in the same `UpdateProperties` call; `ElementStyle::DirtyProperties`, whose only caller that was, is removed.
   - Widgets mark the element whose update consumes their state: `Elements/WidgetTextInput.cpp` (`ShowCursor(true)`, and `OnUpdate` while the cursor blinks), `Elements/WidgetSlider.cpp` (arrow mousedown, and `Update` while an arrow timer runs), `Source/Core/WidgetScroll.cpp` (the same for the scroll container, the scrollbar's parent, whose `ElementScroll::Update` advances the timers), `Elements/WidgetDropDown.cpp` (`selection_dirty` in `OnChildAdd` / `OnChildRemove`, `value_rml_dirty` in `OnValueChange` / `SetSelection`), `Elements/ElementFormControlSelect.cpp` (`OnChildAdd` of a direct child, for `MoveChildren`).
   - `Source/Core/Context.cpp` (`Update`): the root's self bit is reset with its definition flags.
   - Not covered by the bits, as they are consumed in `Render` or layout: `effects_dirty` (`ElementEffects::InstanceEffects` also runs from render), `dirty_transform`, `absolute_offset_dirty`, the stacking context.
   - Layout verify (entry 37) gains one check, compiled only with `RMLUI_ARC_PERF`: after the gated walk of `Context::Update` (per document) and of `ElementDocument::UpdateDocument`, `ArcPerf::VerifyUpdateState` (`Source/Core/{ArcPerf.cpp,ArcPerfInternal.h}`) walks every element of the document and records each one that holds pending update state but would be skipped by the next walk (it or an ancestor below the root has neither bit set). The pass is a `LayoutVerifyPass` with `update_state` set (`Include/RmlUi/Core/ArcPerf.h`): elements checked, violations as mismatches with the `DescribeElement` path, field `pending update`, optimized `skipped` and the pending state as reference. ArcRmlUI logs it as `update verify` in the verify line format. Widget state is not visible to the check: timers, drop-down `selection_dirty` / `value_rml_dirty` and a select's pending `MoveChildren`.
45. Style-sharing candidate count (gate of the sibling style-sharing step, after Firefox Stylo's per-traversal sharing cache), compiled only with `RMLUI_ARC_PERF` and recorded only while a sink is installed.
   - `Source/Core/ElementStyle.{h,cpp}` (`ComputeValues`): at an element's first compute, ArcPerf counts `style first computes`; an element with a parent, no inline properties (so no animated properties), no animations, no pseudo-element type and a definition without `var()` or var shorthands counts as a `style share candidate`, and its `(definition, parent)` tuple as a `style share tuple` the first time it is seen or a `style share hit` after that.
   - The tuple set lives one update walk: `ElementStyle::ClearSharedStyles` runs at the end of `Context::Update` (`Source/Core/Context.cpp`) and of `ElementDocument::UpdateDocument` (`Source/Core/ElementDocument.cpp`, which also covers the load path).
   - `Include/RmlUi/Core/ArcPerf.h`, `Source/Core/ArcPerf.cpp`: the four counters.
46. Cold-open counters, compiled only with `RMLUI_ARC_PERF` and recorded only while a sink is installed. No behaviour change.
   - `Source/Core/Layout/FormattingContext.cpp`, `Source/Core/ArcPerf{.cpp,Internal.h}` (`FormatSiteScope`, `CountFormatCall`): every `FormatIndependent` call counts toward `format calls` and toward the site tagged by the enclosing `FormatSiteScope`: `final flex item loop` (`FlexFormattingContext.cpp`), `final grid item loop` (`GridFormattingContext.cpp`), `final block flow` (`BlockFormattingContext.cpp`), `flex base-size measure`, `flex cross measure`, `shrink-to-fit probe` (`LayoutDetails::ComputeShrinkToFitWidth`), `grid item width` and `grid item measure`; untagged calls (roots, table, absolute) count as `other`. A final-loop call made while a measurement site is open counts as `final item loops nested in a measurement`. The probe sites (`shrink-to-fit`, flex and grid max-content, grid item width, flex base-size and cross measures, grid item measure) also count `formats inside ...`: every format call made while the site is open, including nested sites. Probe call counts are the existing `measure ... misses` of entry 39.

47. Constant data expressions, evaluated without a data model (used by ArcRmlUI's component expander to fold constant `data-if` before the load).
   - `Include/RmlUi/Core/ConstantDataExpression.h`, `Source/Core/DataExpression.cpp` (`EvaluateConstantDataExpression`): parses and runs an expression with the existing `DataParser` and `DataInterpreter` against a given `DataTypeRegister`'s transforms. It returns `Constant` with the value, `ReferencesVariable` when the expression names any data variable (`ev.` addresses included), or `Invalid` for a parse or execution error. The parser and interpreter log nothing in this mode: `DataParser` gains a constant-only mode that records variable references instead of resolving them and suppresses its warnings, and `DataInterpreter` gains a silent mode. A transform called with invalid arguments still logs its own warning (for example `format`, `DataTypeRegister.cpp`).
   - `Source/Core/DataExpression.{h,cpp}` (`DataExpressionInterface`): a constructor taking a `TransformFuncRegister`; `CallTransform` uses it when there is no data model. Model-bound expressions are unchanged.
48. Structural branches are skip-scanned, and the XML tokenizer reads spans (ArcRmlUI cold-open plan step 3). The parsed DOM, the stored inner RML and the line numbers in parse errors are unchanged.
   - `Include/RmlUi/Core/BaseXMLParser.h`, `Source/Core/BaseXMLParser.cpp`: after the open tag of an element with a structural attribute, `SkipInnerXML` reads the branch with the tokenizer's own rules (text with `{{ }}` brackets, comments, CDATA sections, quoted and unquoted attributes, self-closing tags, raw `script`/`style`/`svg` content, line numbers) but builds no strings, attribute maps or decoded values. It ends at the first close tag at the branch's depth, whatever its name, as before; the span up to it is submitted as `InnerXML` data (still the `rmlui-inner-rml` attribute) and the close tag is read normally. The previous capture, which tokenized the branch with the handlers suppressed, is removed. A nested branch is still parsed again when an enclosing branch is instanced; the enclosing parses only scan it.
   - Input that ends inside a branch (unterminated tag, quote, comment, CDATA or raw content) submits the branch up to the end of the input and stops, so the existing `XML parse error on line N` warning reports it; before, the branch was dropped. Malformed input that stops the tokenizer before the end (a bracket error, an empty tag name) still stops the parse without submitting the branch. A structural attribute on an opened raw-content element (`<svg data-if="...">...</svg>`) captures its raw content up to its own close tag; before, the capture state was left open past it. No ArcRmlUI document has one.
   - Tokenizer: `FindString` and `FindWord` return spans and append them in one step, `FindString` finds its terminator with `memchr` when it does not track `{{ }}` brackets (comments, quoted values, close tags, CDATA, raw content); text, which tracks brackets, is still scanned per character, with the bracket parser called only on `{`, `}` and inside brackets; attribute values go through `DecodeRml` only when they contain `&`, the structural-attribute lookup runs only for names starting with `data-`, and raw-content tags are matched case-insensitively without `ToLower`. The parser keeps references to the fixed tag and attribute sets instead of copying them into every instance; `RegisterCDATATag`, `IsCDATATag` and `RegisterInnerXMLAttribute` are removed (`BaseXMLParser` takes the sets in its constructor).
   - `Source/Core/XMLParser.cpp`: the persistent CDATA tags are a `SmallUnorderedSet` passed to the base; `HandleElementStart` / `HandleElementEnd` lower-case the tag name only when it contains an upper-case letter.
   - `Source/Core/Factory.cpp` (`InstanceElementText`): text goes through `DecodeRml` only when it contains `&`.
49. Width-only measurements (ArcRmlUI cold-open plan step 4). Final layouts are unchanged, and measurements return the same widths with less work. Both modes are off during the layout verify reference pass (`LayoutEngine::IsReferencePass`), so `ArcRml.LayoutVerify` compares against the full algorithm.
   - `Source/Core/Layout/FlexFormattingContext.{h,cpp}`: `GetMaxContentSize` / `ComputeMaxContentSize` become `GetMaxContentWidth` / `ComputeMaxContentWidth` and return the width, the only value any caller read (`FlexContainer::GetShrinkToFitWidth` in `ContainerBox.cpp`, `LayoutDetails::GetFlexOrGridMaxContentWidth`, since replaced by `GetFlexOrGridFitContentWidth`, entry 64); the memo kind is `FlexMaxContentWidth` (`LayoutMeasureCache.h`). `ComputeMaxContentWidth` sets `compute_width_only`, as grid's does: a row container returns once its used main size is known, before the item cross measures; a column container returns once its used cross size is known, after the main-size format of auto-height items and the item width measures. Neither runs the final item loop. When any item has an aspect ratio, the full algorithm runs.
   - `Source/Core/Layout/FormattingContext.{h,cpp}` (`FormatShrinkToFitProbe`, `UseShrinkToFitProbeBox`, private `ShrinkToFitProbeScope`): `LayoutDetails::ComputeShrinkToFitWidth` and `GridFormattingContext::ComputeItemContentWidth` make their throwaway format of a block element (the wrapper) through `FormatShrinkToFitProbe`. During that format, an in-flow block-level `flex` or `grid` box (`float: none`, `position` static or relative, not a scroll container, no override box) whose box parent and parent container are the wrapper is a probe box: `FlexFormattingContext::Format` / `GridFormattingContext::Format` return the container after building its box, before resetting scrollbars, formatting items or closing it. The probe mode is inactive for a scroll container wrapper, whose scrollbars depend on the content height. Only the wrapper's own children are probe boxes; boxes deeper in its subtree and every nested measurement format normally, and a nested shrink-to-fit probe installs its own scope and restores the outer one.
   - Exactness: a probe box skips `SetBox`, `OnLayout`, scrollbar changes and the registration of its absolute descendants, and the wrapper's block flow places it with the element's current box (from its last format, or the empty box), so only vertical positions in the wrapper's block formatting context, the probe box's own offset and the wrapper's content and overflow sizes differ from the full probe; none of these is read by the shrink-to-fit width, and of the vertical positions only floats turn into a width. The wrapper's `BlockContainer::GetShrinkToFitWidth` reads the built box's horizontal edges and `FlexContainer` / `GridContainer::GetShrinkToFitWidth` of a probe box (the built width for a `width` length, otherwise the fit-content width of entry 64), the widths of its other child boxes and lines, and the horizontal float positions. Without floats no width depends on a vertical position, since a line's and a box's available width differ only beside floats. With floats it can: a negative margin can move content after the box into the band of a float placed before it. So when the format used a probe box and the wrapper's `FloatedBoxSpace` holds any float afterwards (`HasFloats`, new in `Source/Core/Layout/FloatedBoxSpace.h`), `FormatShrinkToFitProbe` discards the result and formats the wrapper again without probe boxes. The wrapper state left behind by either format is rewritten by the final format, as after a memo hit (entry 39).
   - No memo entry holds a probe box result: probe boxes return before any `LayoutMeasureCache` lookup, `LayoutMeasureCache::Format` is only called with flex, grid and table parent containers, never with a wrapper's block container, and the memoized shrink-to-fit and grid item widths of a wrapper are the values the full probe returns.
50. Font face handles build their glyphs on first use (ArcRmlUI cold-open plan step 5). Replaced by entry 54. Glyph bitmaps and advances, kerning values, font metrics and the base layer's atlas are unchanged; only their build moves from the handle lookup in style computation to the first text measurement, string generation or font-effect configuration of the handle, and a handle that never draws text never builds them.
   - `Source/Core/FontEngineDefault/FreeTypeInterface.{h,cpp}`: `InitialiseFaceHandle` sets the size and generates the metrics only; the new `InitialiseGlyphs` sets the size again (the `FT_Face` is shared by every size of the face) and builds the default ASCII glyphs and the replacement glyph, as `InitialiseFaceHandle` did before.
   - `Source/Core/FontEngineDefault/FontFaceHandleDefault.{h,cpp}`: `Initialize` keeps the metrics and `has_kerning`, and stores `load_default_glyphs`. `EnsureGlyphs` runs `InitialiseGlyphs`, the kerning-pair fill and the base layer and its layer configuration on the first call, at the start of `GetStringWidth`, `GenerateString`, `GenerateLayerConfiguration` (with effects), and on a fallback face before a glyph is taken from it in `GetOrAppendGlyph`.
   - `Include/RmlUi/Core/ArcPerf.h`, `Source/Core/ArcPerf.cpp`, compiled only with `RMLUI_ARC_PERF`: buckets `font.glyphs`, `font.kerning`, `font.layer` inside `EnsureGlyphs`, and the counter `font glyph map builds`.
51. Var-shorthand expansion only where var shorthands exist, and one SVG handle lookup per load (ArcRmlUI cold-open plan step 6). Computed values, rendered SVGs and their textures are unchanged.
   - `Source/Core/ElementDefinition.{h,cpp}` (`HasVarShorthands`): set at construction when the merged stylesheet properties hold a var shorthand. `Source/Core/ElementStyle.cpp` (`ComputeValues`): when variables or var shorthands are dirty, `ExpandVarShorthands` runs only if the definition or the inline properties have var shorthands; otherwise the expanded shorthands are cleared, which is all the expansion did without any, so an element whose new definition has none still drops the old expansion.
   - `Include/RmlUi/SVG/ElementSVG.h`, `Source/SVG/ElementSVG.cpp`: `OnResize` marks the SVG dirty only when the content size or the dp ratio differs from the one of the last load (before, every `OnResize` did). A file-sourced SVG whose `src`, `crop-to-content` and `stroke-width` are unchanged since its handle was obtained takes the intrinsic size from that handle: `GetIntrinsicDimensions` does not load, and `EnsureSourceLoaded` computes the object-fit rectangle first and requests the handle once at its size, the key the second request of the previous code produced. After a source change, and for inline SVG data, the load still requests at the box size and again at the fitted size when it differs. Attribute strings are read by reference and the inline wrapper iterates the attributes without copying them.
   - `Source/SVG/SVGCache.cpp`: the handle key is built once, by moving the source id into it, and used for both the lookup and the insert; file paths are moved into the key; inline data is passed by pointer instead of being copied before parsing.
52. Size-only measurement formats (ArcRmlUI cold-open round 2 plan step 1). Final layouts are unchanged, and measurements return the same box and last-line baseline with less work. The mode is off during the layout verify reference pass (`LayoutEngine::IsReferencePass`), so `ArcRml.LayoutVerify` compares against the full algorithm.
   - `Source/Core/Layout/LayoutMeasureCache.{h,cpp}` (`SizeOnlyScope`, `IsSizeOnly`): the size-only mode belongs to the active pass memo (entry 39), so a nested pass (`ElementUtilities::FormatElement` from an `OnLayout`) starts in full mode, and the reference pass, which has no active memo, never enters it. `LayoutMeasureCache::Format` runs its format in size-only mode unless the measured element has `overflow: auto` on either axis. The `Format` memo key gains the mode, so a size-only result never answers a full-mode lookup.
   - `Source/Core/Layout/FormattingContext.{h,cpp}`: `FormatIndependent` turns the mode off for the subtree of every element with `overflow: auto` on either axis (its scrollbars depend on the overflow of its content) and restores it afterwards. Every non-replaced `overflow: auto` box reaches layout through `FormatIndependent`, because a non-visible overflow makes a box an independent formatting context. A `LayoutMeasureCache::Format` nested below such a box is size-only again: it returns only the box and baseline, and the enclosing full-mode container formats the item again in its final item loop. `UseSizeOnlyFormat`: in size-only mode, a block-level `display: flex` / `display: grid` box that is not a scroll container (`LayoutDetails::IsScrollContainer`) is formatted size-only.
   - `Source/Core/Layout/FlexFormattingContext.{h,cpp}`, `Source/Core/Layout/GridFormattingContext.{h,cpp}`: a size-only container returns its content size once it is final, flex after the used cross size, grid after the container content box, with the same values and operation order as the full path, and then still runs `Close` (`SubmitBox`, positioned elements, `OnLayout`, element baseline). It skips the line alignment, item placement and final item formats (flex), the track alignment, out-of-flow registration and final item formats (grid), and so the item overflow and the container baseline. Absolutely positioned and relative children of a flex container are still registered, since that happens while its items are collected.
   - Exactness: inside a measurement, the skipped results are read only by readers outside the measured value. Overflow feeds `SubmitBox`'s scrollable overflow rectangle and the propagated visible overflow, which only `CatchOverflow` of an `overflow: auto` box turns into a size (excluded above), and float overflow extents (`FloatedBoxSpace::PlaceFloat`), which only feed overflow; float placement and float shrink-to-fit widths use margin boxes. The element baseline is read only by `InlineLevelBox_Atomic` (`InlineLevelBox.cpp`) for `inline-flex` / `inline-grid`, which stay full; `FlexContainer` and `GridContainer` report no last-line baseline, so a measured block's baseline (`BlockContainer::GetBaselineOfLastLine`) is unchanged. Item boxes, offsets, lines and scrollbars that the skipped item loops wrote are rewritten by the final format, as after a memo hit (entry 39); a size-only container's own box is written by its `Close`.
53. Async jobs for the RmlUi thread (ArcRmlUI cold-open round 2 plan step 2). No consumer yet; nothing changes until a feature launches a job.
   - `Include/RmlUi/Core/AsyncJobInterface.h`, `Source/Core/Core.cpp`: `AsyncJob` is a function that runs on any thread and returns an `AsyncInstall`, a function that runs on the RmlUi thread. `AsyncJobOwner::Launch` hands the job to the `AsyncJobInterface` set with `SetAsyncJobInterface` (`Include/RmlUi/Core/Core.h`), or runs it inline when none is set; the finished job's install is queued under a mutex together with a weak reference to the owner's token. `ProcessAsyncResults` takes the queue under the lock and runs, on the calling RmlUi thread, the installs whose owner is still alive and has not called `AsyncJobOwner::Invalidate` since the launch, and returns how many ran. Owners are created, invalidated and destroyed on the RmlUi thread. Jobs record no ArcPerf data, whose sink and scope stack are RmlUi-thread globals.
   - `Rml::Shutdown` asserts that no job launched through the interface is still running, then drops the queued results before tearing down, and clears the interface with the others. The application waits for its jobs before calling it.
   - A job's captures are destroyed on the thread that ran it, so they must not hold RmlUi objects or references to them (elements, handles, `SharedPtr`s whose last release would destroy an RmlUi-thread object on the worker); install captures are destroyed on the RmlUi thread. No job may be launched after the host has waited for its jobs during shutdown.
   - `Include/RmlUi/Core.h` includes the new header.
54. Light-hinted fonts with glyphs built by async jobs (ArcRmlUI cold-open round 2 plan step 3). Replaces the glyph build of entry 50. Glyph shapes and advances change once, because every glyph is hinted with `FT_LOAD_TARGET_LIGHT`; layout and drawing use the same advances. Text whose glyphs are not built yet takes its full width in layout and draws nothing until they arrive.
   - `Source/Core/FontEngineDefault/FreeTypeInterface.{h,cpp}`: every glyph load uses `FT_LOAD_TARGET_LIGHT`, including the `x` glyph of the metrics, and renders with `FT_RENDER_MODE_LIGHT`. `InitialiseFaceHandle` also returns the handle's `x_scale` and bitmap scaling factor (`FontAdvanceScale`, `FontTypes.h`). `GetAdvance` reads the advance from the font tables with `FT_Get_Advance(FT_LOAD_NO_SCALE)` and computes `FT_PIX_ROUND(FT_MulFix(advance, x_scale))`, the advance the light-hinted autohinter gives the loaded glyph, without loading it. `RenderGlyphs` creates its own `FT_Library` and `FT_New_Memory_Face` over the face data, loads and renders the requested characters, and destroys both; it touches no shared FreeType state and runs on any thread. `CreateReplacementGlyph` builds the procedural replacement glyph. `InitialiseGlyphs`, `AppendGlyph`, `BuildGlyphMap` and the ASCII preload are deleted.
   - `Source/Core/FontEngineDefault/FontFace.{h,cpp}`, `FontFamily.{h,cpp}`, `FontProvider.{h,cpp}`: a face keeps the memory it was loaded from and its face index with the named instance (`(named_instance_index << 16) | face_index`), and passes them to its handles. That memory lives until `Rml::Shutdown`, after the application has waited for its jobs. The `load_default_glyphs` parameter of `GetHandle` and `Initialize` is deleted.
   - `Source/Core/FontEngineDefault/FontFaceHandleDefault.{h,cpp}`: `GetCharacter` resolves a character once per handle into its advance and the handle that builds its glyph: this handle when the face has the character, otherwise the first fallback face handle that builds that character's own glyph (whose advance it takes; a fallback whose entry for it is a replacement or another fallback is skipped), otherwise the replacement glyph. A character this handle has is added to the handle's request list; the map of resolved characters is the set that keeps a character from being requested twice, also while its job runs. `GetStringWidth` and `GenerateString` advance by the resolved advance; `GenerateString` draws only glyphs that are installed, since a layer holds boxes only for installed glyphs, so a pending glyph emits no quads, and the replacement glyph, created with the base layer, keeps the base layer atlas non-empty, so no layer texture callback returns false while glyphs are pending. `SubmitGlyphRequests` launches one job per handle with requests (one face and size) through the handle's `AsyncJobOwner`; the job captures the face data, face index, size and characters, and returns an install that captures the handle and the rendered glyphs. The install adds the glyphs, marks the layers dirty and runs `UpdateLayersOnDirty`, which bumps the version so text geometry regenerates, and then gives every handle that resolved one of those characters to this handle as fallback a weak copy of the glyph, and updates its layers. A requested character the job built no glyph for (the job could not create its library or face, or set the size) keeps its advance and is drawn as the replacement glyph, in this handle and in the handles that use it as fallback, with one warning per job. A destroyed handle drops its pending install with its owner token and leaves the request list. Kerning stays `FT_Get_Kerning` on the UI thread, which loads no glyph; the ASCII kerning cache is filled on the first kerning lookup of a face with kerning.
   - `Source/Core/Context.cpp`: `Context::Update`, `Context::Render` and `Context::LoadDocument` call `FontFaceHandleDefault::SubmitGlyphRequests` at their end, so characters first resolved while rendering (a `text-overflow` ellipsis, decorator text, the drag clone) are submitted in the same pump.
   - `Source/Core/FontEffectBlur.cpp`, `FontEffectGlow.cpp`, `FontEffectOutline.cpp`: `GetGlyphMetrics` skips a glyph without bitmap data, so no effect texture reads a null bitmap.
   - `Include/RmlUi/Core/ArcPerf.h`, `Source/Core/ArcPerf.cpp`, compiled only with `RMLUI_ARC_PERF`: the buckets `font.glyphs`, `font.kerning`, `font.layer` and the counter `font glyph map builds` are deleted. The install records the bucket `font.glyph_install` and the counters `font glyph batches` and `font glyphs installed`. While a sink is installed, the install also compares each glyph's advance with the advance layout used, logs every difference as a warning and logs one `Font glyph install` line per batch with the number of differences.
55. SVG textures rasterized by async jobs for every `SVGCache` consumer (ArcRmlUI cold-open round 2 plan step 4). Replaces the rasterizing texture callback of entry 31 and the intrinsic-size handle lookup of entry 51. Rendered pixels are unchanged once installed. A newly loaded SVG draws nothing until its job's result is installed; when its size, colour, stroke width or crop changes, an element or decorator keeps drawing its last installed texture until the new one installs (typically one frame). A request whose render size rounds to zero draws nothing, and an element whose `src` value or inline SVG source changes draws nothing until the new source installs; a source that fails to load draws nothing and logs a warning, so a colour transition steps through the colours whose rasters arrive in time instead of every frame's colour.
   - `Source/SVG/SVGCache.{h,cpp}`: a new texture entry launches one job through its `AsyncJobOwner`. The job reads the file bytes through the reader set with `SVG::SetFileReader` (`Include/RmlUi/SVG/SVGFileReader.h`; it must be thread-safe) unless the document entry already holds them, parses its own `lunasvg::Document`, applies the colour and stroke width, rasterizes (cropped with `crop-to-content`), swaps red and blue, and returns an install that stores the bitmap in the entry and marks it ready. The install also stores, when not known yet, the read bytes, the intrinsic size and `follows_current_colour` in the document entry and the cropped size in the texture entry, and logs read, parse and render failures. Releasing the entry destroys its owner, so a pending install is dropped. The texture callback only uploads the stored bitmap; consumers never draw a texture that is not ready, so no callback returns false while waiting. Entries with a zero size launch no job and never become ready. Documents and texture entries are held by `UniquePtr`, so the install and the callback reach their entry directly. Until `follows_current_colour` is known, texture and handle keys include the element's colour; once it is known to be false, a request reuses an existing entry of the same size, crop and stroke width whatever its colour key, or keys on no colour. `GetHandle` takes `require_intrinsic`: when set and the intrinsic size (or the cropped size) is not known, the source is read and parsed on the calling thread for the size only, and that parse is not used for rasterization. `SVGData` exposes `IsReady` and `GetIntrinsicDimensions` and no longer copies the intrinsic size.
   - `Source/SVG/ElementSVG.cpp`, `Include/RmlUi/SVG/ElementSVG.h`: an `<svg>` with both `width` and `height` attributes requests no handle in `GetIntrinsicDimensions`; one without both requests it with `require_intrinsic`. `OnRender` draws the last ready handle with its geometry (`ready_handle`, `ready_geometry`) and replaces it when the newest requested handle becomes ready; a newer request releases the previous pending handle, which drops its install. A request that yields no handle or a zero-size handle (`SVGData::HasZeroSize`), or whose `src` value or inline wrapper source differs from the last load (`loaded_source`), clears the drawn one. The element first requests a zero-size handle, which launches no job, to read the intrinsic size the document already knows and request the `object-fit` size directly. When the size is unknown, it requests the texture at its box size and sets `awaiting_intrinsic`; once the install has stored the size, its next `OnRender` rebuilds the geometry and requests the texture at the `object-fit` size, which for `fill` is the same entry. Inline SVG data marks the source dirty on `SetInnerRML` and on any attribute change, since every attribute is part of the generated wrapper, and the old inline handle is dropped only when its source changed.
   - `Source/SVG/DecoratorSVG.{h,cpp}`: never needs the intrinsic size. The decorator maps each element to its live data; new element data generated while the old data is still alive (`ElementEffects::ReloadEffectsData` releases it afterwards) takes over the old data's last ready handle unless the new handle has a zero size, and `RenderElement` draws the new handle once ready, otherwise that handle.
   - `ThirdParty/lunasvg/source/graphics.{h,cpp}`: `FontFaceCache::addFontFace` and `getFontFace` lock a mutex, since the UI-thread parse and jobs can use the font cache at the same time.
   - `Include/RmlUi/Core/ArcPerf.h`, `Source/Core/ArcPerf.cpp`, compiled only with `RMLUI_ARC_PERF`: the install records the bucket `svg.rasterize` and the counter `svg rasterizations`; `svg documents parsed` is counted by the install and by the calling-thread parse. The new bucket `svg.upload` covers the texture callback, which counts `textures svg`.
56. Data expressions share their compiled program within one document load (ArcRmlUI cold-open round 2 plan step 5). Views, controllers, their values and the warnings they log are unchanged.
   - `Source/Core/DataExpression.{h,cpp}` (`DataParseMemo`, installed by `Context::LoadDocument(Stream*)` in `Source/Core/Context.cpp`): a memo keyed by the expression text and whether it is an assignment holds the compiled `Program` and the variable name of each address slot. A later parse of the same key resolves those names for its element without logging; when every slot resolves it takes the shared program and the resolved addresses, otherwise it parses in full as before, with the same warnings and slot indices. Only parses whose every slot resolved are stored. A nested load installs its own memo. Views created inside `LoadDocument`, including rows and branches instanced by its data-model update, use the memo; views created after `LoadDocument` returns (later rows, branches, `SetInnerRML`) parse in full.
   - `Source/Core/DataModel.{h,cpp}` (`ResolveAddress`): while a memo is installed, the split of an address string is memoized; `log_missing` lets the memo hit check resolve silently.
   - `DataExpression` no longer stores its expression text: `Parse` takes it, and `DataParser` reads it by reference. `Source/Core/ElementUtilities.cpp` (`ApplyDataViewsControllers`) copies each binding's expression once and checks once whether its type is structural. `Source/Core/DataControllerDefault.cpp` follows the `Parse` signature.
   - `DataView::GetVariableNameList` and `DataExpression::GetVariableNameList` are removed. `DataView::ForEachVariableAddress` (`Source/Core/DataView.h`, overrides in `Source/Core/DataViewDefault.{h,cpp}`) visits the addresses, and `DataViews::Update` and `ReleaseRemovedViews` (`Source/Core/DataView.cpp`) key the variable map by each address's first name, as before. `DataViewAlias` visits no address: it was registered under its alias name, and its `Update` does nothing, so no update depended on it. With `RMLUI_ARC_PERF` detailed attribution, alias views are listed as `(no variables)`.
   - ArcRmlUI's component expander (`Components/ArcRmlComponentExpander.cpp`) folds constant bindings before the load with `EvaluateConstantDataExpression` (entry 47): `data-attr-*` into the attribute, `data-style-*` into the `style` attribute after its declarations, `data-class-*` into `class`, and text whose `{{ }}` expressions are all constant into the text `DataViewText` would set.
57. File textures (`<img>`, `fill-image`, image decorators and sprite sheets) are decoded by async jobs (ArcRmlUI compiled-documents plan step 1). Replaces the synchronous `RenderInterface::LoadTexture`. Pixels are unchanged once installed. A file texture draws nothing until its decode is installed (typically within one or two frames). An `<img>` with both `width` and `height` attributes takes its size from them without waiting, also when the file fails to load (upstream then gave 0×0); one without both reports the texture size it knows so far (0×0 while decoding) and relayouts once the decode is installed.
   - `Include/RmlUi/Core/TextureFileDecoder.h` (new, included by `Include/RmlUi/Core.h`): `SetTextureFileDecoder` installs the host function that turns a source path into premultiplied RGBA8 pixels and their size. It is called from async jobs on any thread, so it must be thread-safe. `Rml::Shutdown` clears it (`Source/Core/Core.cpp`).
   - `Source/Core/TextureDatabase.{h,cpp}` (`FileTextureDatabase`): an entry stores its source and a load state (unrequested, pending, ready, failed). `IsReady` and `GetDimensions` request the decode on first use: one job per source through the database's `AsyncJobOwner` (entry 53), capturing the source and a copy of the decoder. Its install, on the RmlUi thread, stores the size and pixels and marks the entry ready, or marks it failed and logs `Could not load texture` once; an install whose entry was released since the launch (generation counter) is dropped, and destroying the database drops every pending install. `GetHandle` uploads the stored pixels with `RenderInterface::GenerateTexture` on first draw and frees them; it is only reached for a ready or failed entry. Releasing an uploaded texture (`ReleaseTexture`, `ReleaseAllTextures`) returns the entry to unrequested, so the next use decodes it again; failed entries and entries not yet uploaded are left as they are.

58. Compiled binary style sheets; `<link>` style sheets load only from them (ArcRmlUI compiled-documents plan step 2). Until the host installs a reader, a document's `<link>` style sheets do not load and log an error. Inline `<style>` sheets still parse as text.
   - `Include/RmlUi/Core/StyleSheetBinary.h` (new, included by `Include/RmlUi/Core.h`), `Source/Core/StyleSheetBinary.{h,cpp}` (new): `WriteStyleSheetBinary` serializes a `StyleSheetContainer` parsed in compile mode: the media blocks (query properties and modifier), each style sheet's specificity offset, its node tree with every compound selector field, including `:not()` selector trees and their leaf list, each node's properties, custom properties and `var()` shorthands, and the keyframes. Properties and shorthands are stored by name. Values without pointers (none, numbers, strings, vectors, colours) are stored typed; values holding pointers (transform, transitions, animations, decorators, filters, font effects, colour stops, box shadows, grid, calc) are stored as the declaration they came from. Every property also stores its unit, specificity, `!important` flag, parser index, whether it has a definition, and its source line and rule name. `ReadStyleSheetBinary` rebuilds the container: it resolves names through the style sheet specification (the media query specification for media blocks), re-parses each stored declaration and takes the one longhand it stored, checking that the type and unit still match, sets the source path of every property to the path it is given, and recomputes the keyframe property ids. An unknown property or shorthand name, a declaration that no longer yields its property, or malformed data makes the body unusable, and it returns null with the reason. `GetCompiledRegistryHash` hashes, on its first call after `Rml::Initialise`, the registered property and shorthand names with their parsers, parser parameters, preserve-quotes flags, shorthand items and aliases (`PropertySpecification::GetRegistrySignature`), the same for the media query specification, the persistent CDATA tags and the structural data view attributes; `Rml::Shutdown` resets it.

A compile-mode parse keeps a `StyleSheetCompileRecord` on the container: for each rule source and each keyframe block, the declaration (name and value, without `!important`) that set each property, following the `!important` precedence of `PropertyDictionary::Import`; a longhand set by a shorthand keeps the shorthand name and value. A compile-mode parse fails with an error naming the file and line on `@decorator`, `@spritesheet` and `@font-face`. `PostprocessKeyframes` and the media query specification (`GetMediaQuerySpecification`) are exposed on `StyleSheetParser`.

A path not ending in `.rcss`, a missing reader, a failed read or an unusable body logs an error and loads nothing. The path-keyed cache is unchanged. `Rml::Shutdown` clears the reader.

In editor builds `Compile/ArcRmlDocumentCompiler.{h,cpp}` compiles them: the component expander (a new one per document, which fails the compile on any expander error) and `CompileDocument` for documents, a compile-mode `StyleSheetContainer::LoadStyleSheetContainer` and `WriteStyleSheetBinary` for style sheets. The UI thread compiles every missing, unusable or changed file once at start, installs the compiled style sheet reader after `Rml::Initialise`, and compiles a missing or unusable file when it is opened; packaged builds only read the files. The document read and decode are added to the load's `compiled.read` bucket.
61. `px` follows the dp ratio; values the fork resolves to device pixels carry the internal unit `devpx` (ArcRmlUI scaling plan step 2). At a dp ratio of 1 layouts are unchanged.
   - `Include/RmlUi/Core/Unit.h`: `Unit::DEVICE_PX` (`1ull << 34`) joins `LENGTH`; `DP_SCALABLE_LENGTH` is now `PX | DP | PPI_UNIT`. No parser suffix table has an entry for it, so authored CSS never produces it. `Source/Core/TypeConverter.cpp` writes it as `devpx`. `Source/Core/StyleSheetBinary.cpp`: the `.rcssc` reader rejects a property stored with it.
   - `Source/Core/ComputeProperty.cpp` (`ComputeLength`): `PX` resolves to `px × dp_ratio`, `DEVICE_PX` unscaled. `Source/Core/ElementStyle.cpp`: `ComputeLength(value, element)` fetches the dp ratio for `PX` through `DP_SCALABLE_LENGTH`, and `ResolveNumericValue` returns only `DEVICE_PX` raw. `ComputeBorderWidth` rounding is unchanged, so a 2px border is 3 device px at 1.333 (owner-accepted exception to the Chrome comparison, 2026-10-09). Media query `width`/`height` comparisons (`Source/Core/StyleSheetContainer.cpp`) now compare the device viewport against scaled `px`, as browsers do. Image, SVG, nine-patch and tiled-decorator intrinsic sizes keep their dp multiply and now agree with `px`.
   - `Source/Core/Element.cpp` (`OnDpRatioChangeRecursive`): a dp ratio change dirties properties in `DP_SCALABLE_LENGTH` units (now including `PX`), box-shadow and text-shadow lists, transforms, decorators, filters, grid definitions and unresolved `var()` values. Each running or held animation prepares its keys again and its current value is applied (`ElementAnimation::OnDpRatioChange`, `Source/Core/ElementAnimation.{h,cpp}`; the keys keep their unprepared values in `key_sources`). `PrepareTransforms` prepares a copy of each key's transform: upstream prepared the transform shared with the style sheet in place, which wrote resolved device values into the keyframes and the element's own `transform`.
   - `Source/Core/DecoratorTiled.{h,cpp}`: a tile's `align` keeps its authored value (`NumericValue`) and a `px` value is resolved with the element when geometry is generated; `Tile::GenerateGeometry` takes the element instead of its computed values (`DecoratorTiledImage.cpp`, `DecoratorTiledBox.cpp`, `DecoratorTiledHorizontal.cpp`, `DecoratorTiledVertical.cpp`).
   - `Source/Core/ElementScroll.cpp`: the Fluent scrollbar metrics are Chrome's CSS-pixel constants; `GetMetrics` multiplies them by the dp ratio before rounding, as Chrome scales them by the device scale factor (15px track: 30 device px at 2.0), and the rounded results are set as `DEVICE_PX`. `ElementScroll::OnDpRatioChange`, called from `Element::OnDpRatioChangeRecursive`, reapplies them when the dp ratio changes. The arrow decorator is positioned and sized in percentages of the arrow box, so it follows the scaled arrow.
   - `Unit::PX` sites, classified. Authored (scale): the `px` suffix of `PropertyParserNumber.cpp` and `PropertyParserCalc.cpp`; the zero units of the length parsers (`StyleSheetSpecification.cpp`, `PropertyParserDecorator.cpp`, `PropertyParserTransform.cpp`) and the zero fill of missing transform terms (`PropertyParserTransform.cpp`); the default units of the `TranslateX/Y/Z`, `Translate2D/3D` constructors (`TransformPrimitive.h`); the zero blur default of `drop-shadow()` (`FilterDropShadow.cpp`); the tiled-decorator `align` (above); parse-time `calc()` folding (`FoldCalcExpression`). Fork-produced (now `DEVICE_PX`): compute-time `calc()` leaves (`CalcExpression.cpp`, `ResolveCalcLengths`, which now also resolves `px` leaves); mixed-unit interpolation (`ElementAnimation.cpp`, `InterpolateNumericValue`); transform preparation and its zero fill (`TransformUtilities.cpp`, `PrepareVisitor`, `ConvertToGenericTypeVisitor`, and the `ResolveWidth/Height/Length` fast paths); resolved box-shadow lengths (`GeometryBoxShadow.cpp`); measured values written back as properties: drag handles (`ElementHandle.cpp`), drag clone position and margins and cursor proxy border widths (`Context.cpp`), the dp-scaled Fluent scrollbar metrics (`ElementScroll.cpp`, above), the select box height (`Elements/WidgetDropDown.cpp`). Unit handlers: `ComputeProperty.cpp`, `ElementStyle.cpp`, `TypeConverter.cpp`.
   - Not scaled: font effects (`font-effect`) read their lengths as raw numbers when instanced, for `px` and `dp` alike; the default `font-size` of an element without one (`DefaultComputedValues`, 12) stays 12 device px. Font face handles take the integer part of the font size (`ElementStyle.cpp`, `GetFontFaceHandle`), so at a non-integer dp ratio text is narrower than in Chrome (1.5–3% at 1.333). This is an owner-accepted exception to the Chrome comparison (2026-10-09), alongside border rounding; fractional sizes need a float size in `FontEngineInterface::GetFontFaceHandle` (ArcRmlUI TODO, "Fork CSS gaps").
   - ArcRmlUI (`Thread/ArcRmlLayoutDump.cpp`): the html converts `px` and `dp` lengths with one pass (`× dp_ratio`) and writes `devpx` unscaled as `px`; `width`/`height` attributes of `img` and `svg` are multiplied by `dp_ratio`, and an `img` with neither gets its device-pixel intrinsic size as attributes. The `inputs` of the layout json write `devpx` as `px`. The `units` string records the contract.
62. Keyed `data-for` (ArcRmlUI damage numbers plan step 1, after Vue `:key` and React keys). A `data-for` without `data-key` behaves as before.
   - `Source/Core/DataViewDefault.{h,cpp}` (`DataViewFor`): `data-key="<iterator>.<member path>"` on the `data-for` element keys its rows. `Initialize` rejects any other form (an identifier path after the iterator name) with an error, and the view is not added. `data-key` is not copied to the rows. On each update the key of entry `i` is read as `container[i].<member path>` and compared by its string value. A row whose key is kept at the same index is untouched. A kept row at a new index keeps its element in the DOM, and its subtree's aliases, views and controllers are recreated in place against the new index, so its classes, local style and running animations survive. A new key gets a fresh row, inserted before the next kept row (or the anchor); a missing key's row is removed. When kept keys change their relative order, every row from the first out-of-order key on is recreated fresh. An entry whose key repeats an earlier one, or cannot be read, gets no row; each case logs one error per update. On its first update a keyed view checks its row content (the compiled sub-stream, or the `rmlui-inner-rml` text); a row containing a structural view (`data-for`, `data-if`) logs an error and the view creates no rows. The check waits for the first update because the inner RML is attached after the anchor's views are initialized (`XMLNodeHandlerDefault.cpp`). Row creation is shared by both paths (`InstanceRow`, `InsertRowAliases`).
   - `Source/Core/DataModel.{h,cpp}` (`RebindSubtree`): for an element and its descendants bound to the same model, removes their views (after `DataView::RestoreElementSource`), controllers and aliases, lets the caller insert the root's aliases, then applies data views and controllers again in tree order, without detaching anything. `DataViewText` keeps the text it was initialized from and restores it there, so the recreated view parses the `{{ }}` template; the restored text is set again by the view's first update.
   - `Source/Core/DataView.{h,cpp}` (`DataViews`): a view removed during an update pass (its element removed or rebound) is not updated for the rest of that pass. `DataViewFor` and `DataViewIf` use sort offset -1000, so a structural view updates before the views on the rows and branches it generates, which share its depth; before, the order among them was unspecified, and a row view could read an entry the `data-for` was about to remove.
   - `Source/Core/XMLEventStream.{h,cpp}`: `HasStructuralDataView` for a compiled sub-stream and for inner RML text.
   - `Source/Core/DataExpression.cpp` (`DataExpressionTable`): `world` reads its value as a common view expression, for the `data-world` view of damage numbers plan step 2. `data-key` is a path, not an expression, and is not in the table.
   - ArcRmlUI: `Compile/ArcRmlCompiledFile.h`: `ArcRmlCompiledFormatVersion` 2; older `.rmlc` and `.rcssc` files are unusable and are compiled again.
63. `data-world` world-anchored elements (ArcRmlUI damage numbers plan step 2). Documents without `data-world` are unchanged.
   - `Include/RmlUi/Core/WorldAnchors.h` (included by `Core.h`), `Source/Core/WorldAnchors.cpp`, `Source/Core/WorldAnchorSet.h`: `SetWorldProjector(Context&, WorldProjector)` installs the host projector of a context (a world point as `Vector3<double>` in, a point in context device pixels and an in-front flag out); `ReprojectWorldAnchors(Context&)` places every live `data-world` element of the context again and returns whether any translation or visibility changed. The context owns its anchor set (`Context::world_anchors`, created on first use, destroyed after the context's data models). A view registers itself in `Initialize` and leaves the set in `Release`; reprojection skips and drops views whose element is gone or that were removed (`DataView::IsRemoved`, new).
   - `Source/Core/DataViewDefault.{h,cpp}` (`DataViewWorld`), registered as `world` in `Source/Core/Factory.cpp`: `data-world="<expr>"` is a common view expression (seeded from the compiled table, entry 62) whose value is the string `"x y z"` in centimetres. The element's `transform` is set to `translate(x, y)` in `devpx` (entry 61) with the projected context point, so the element's layout position must be the context origin; no layout runs. The element is `visibility: hidden` when the point is behind the camera, the context has no projector or the projector has no camera, and before its first update. A value that is not three finite numbers separated by whitespace hides the element and logs one error per view. Placement runs in `Initialize`, `Update` and `ReprojectWorldAnchors`; properties are written only when the translation or visibility changes.

64. Keyframe `var()` sees the animated element's inline custom properties, and absolutely positioned (and other shrink-to-fit) boxes never shrink below their preferred minimum width (ArcRmlUI damage numbers plan step 4b). Equipment and Gallery layouts are unchanged.
   - `Source/Core/ElementStyle.{h,cpp}`: `PropertySources::keyframe_element_inline_properties`. `ResolveKeyFrameProperty` still passes the keyframe block as the inline properties (its var shorthands and placeholders resolve as before) and now also the element's inline properties. `GetLocalCustomProperty(const PropertySources&, ...)` takes a custom property from the block, else from the element's inline properties (`data-style---dx`, `style`), cascaded against the element definition as before. Before, an inline custom property of the animated element was invisible to its keyframes (`Invalid substitution, variable '--dx' not defined`). Keyframe values are still resolved once when the animation starts (`Element::HandleAnimationProperty`); a later change of the variable does not re-resolve them.
   - `Source/Core/Layout/LayoutDetails.{h,cpp}` (`ComputeShrinkToFitWidth`, new `GetFlexOrGridFitContentWidth` replacing `GetFlexOrGridMaxContentWidth` of entry 38, new `GetMinContentWidth`): CSS 2.1 §10.3.7, min(max(preferred minimum, available), preferred), with the min-content width as the preferred minimum (never above the preferred width). When the preferred width of a block container exceeds the available width, the element is formatted again under a zero content width and that shrink-to-fit width is its min-content width (`GetMinContentWidth`, the probe `GridFormattingContext::ComputeItemContentWidth` uses for min-content). A flex or grid element takes `GetFlexOrGridFitContentWidth`: its max-content width when that fits the available width or the available width is negative, otherwise max(min(min-content, max-content), available). Before, the result was min(preferred, available), so a `white-space: nowrap` span in a 0×0 containing block got width 0.
   - `Source/Core/Layout/ContainerBox.{h,cpp}`: `FlexContainer` / `GridContainer::GetShrinkToFitWidth` of a box without a `width` length (a flex or grid box inside a measured block container) return `GetFlexOrGridFitContentWidth` for the width an auto width would fill (`ContainerBox::GetAvailableContentWidth`, new: the containing block width minus border, padding and non-auto margins, before the `min-width` / `max-width` clamp). Under the max-content probe that width is the containing block plus 10000 px, so the result stays the max-content width; under the zero-width probe it is the min-content width. Before, both always returned the max-content width, so a block with a flex or grid child took the child's max-content width as its min-content width.
   - `Source/Core/Layout/GridFormattingContext.{h,cpp}`: `ComputeItemContentWidth` gives a flex or grid item `GetFlexOrGridFitContentWidth` for its constraint: the min-content width under a min-content constraint, the max-content width under a max-content constraint, and the fit-content width for a definite available width minus the item's padding and border. Before, it was always the max-content width. `GetMinContentWidth` (memo kind `GridMinContentWidth`) runs the max-content path (`ComputeIntrinsicWidth`) with the columns sized under a min-content constraint: `Format` uses `indefinite_width` as the available width of an indefinite container width.
   - `Source/Core/Layout/FlexFormattingContext.{h,cpp}`: `GetMinContentWidth` (memo kind `FlexMinContentWidth`) builds the width from the in-flow items' min-content contributions, as Chrome does: an item's `width` length (or the built width of a replaced or aspect-ratio item), otherwise its `LayoutDetails::GetMinContentWidth`, clamped by its `min-width` / `max-width` lengths, plus its horizontal padding, border and margins. Percentages resolve against an indefinite width (`auto`, `none` and 0). A single-line row container sums the contributions and the column gaps between them; a multi-line row container and a column container take the largest. `flex-basis` does not enter.
   - `Source/Core/Layout/LayoutMeasureCache.{h,cpp}`, `Include/RmlUi/Core/ArcPerf.h`, `Source/Core/ArcPerf.cpp`, `Source/Core/ArcPerfInternal.h`: memo kinds `FlexMinContentWidth` and `GridMinContentWidth`, format sites `FlexMinContent` and `GridMinContent`, counters `formats inside flex/grid min-content` and `measure flex/grid min-content hits/misses`.
   - Not covered: the fit-content width of a flex or grid box is not clamped by its own `min-width` / `max-width` (a block container's shrink-to-fit width is), and the flex max-content width still comes from the flex algorithm with the items' flex bases.
65. Virtual `data-for` (ArcRmlUI virtual lists plan step 1). A `data-for` without `data-virtual` behaves as before.
   - `Source/Core/DataViewDefault.{h,cpp}` (`DataViewFor`): `data-virtual` on a `data-for` element (alone or with `data-key`) creates rows only for a window of entries. `data-virtual` is not copied to the rows. The anchor's parent is the scroll container; after the first layout, a parent whose `overflow-y` is not `auto` or `scroll` logs an error with the anchor's address and the view creates no rows. Before the first layout the view creates one row; after each layout it measures the first existing row's margin box, takes the container's `row-gap` / `column-gap` (flex and grid containers only), and computes the column count as `max(1, floor((content width + column gap) / (item width + column gap)))` from the client width minus horizontal padding. The window is the visible lines (scroll top minus top padding, client height) plus one client height of lines before and after; it starts on a line boundary. Rows outside the window are removed, rows entering it are created at the window edges, kept rows stay. A keyed virtual view reads keys only for entries inside the window, so a repeated key outside it is not detected. Two spacer elements (`div.rml-virtual-spacer`, inline `width: 100%`, `flex-shrink: 0`, `grid-column: 1 / -1`) are inserted before the first row and after the last row; each is `lines × line size − row gap` device pixels high (line size = item height + row gap), or `display: none` when it covers no line, so the scroll height and the position of every visible row match the full list. The window is recomputed when the container variable is dirty, on the container's `scroll` event (the listener only requests a view update and the next context update; rows never change inside the dispatch), and after a layout that changed the item size, column count, client size or scroll position (including a silent clamp). Spacers and rows are not removed when the view is released; the scroll listener is. Rows that leave the window lose focus, hover and animations. Variable item sizes, horizontal virtual lists and other children of the container besides the rows are not supported. The non-virtual path shares `UpdateRows` and the range form of `UpdateKeyed` with the window `[0, size)` and returns true when it created or removed rows.
   - `Source/Core/DataView.{h,cpp}` (`DataView::OnLayout`, `DataViews::RequestUpdate`, `AddLayoutObserver`, `UpdateAfterLayout`): a view can request one update outside variable dirtiness (run in the first pass of the next `DataViews::Update`) and register to be called after layout. Removed views leave both lists in `OnElementRemove`.
   - `Source/Core/DataModel.{h,cpp}`: `RequestViewUpdate`, `AddLayoutObserver`, `UpdateAfterLayout` forward to the model's views.
   - `Source/Core/Context.cpp` (`Context::Update`): after the documents' layout, every data model's layout observers run; when any of them requested an update, the data models update and the documents are styled and laid out again in the same `Context::Update`, at most 8 rounds (then a warning, and the rest waits for the next update, which is requested).
   - ArcRmlUI: `Components/ArcRmlComponentExpander.cpp` passes `data-virtual` from a component tag to its host element, like `data-for`.
66. `asset:` texture sources: Unreal textures loaded by the host and drawn from the GPU (ArcRmlUI asset textures plan step 1). Sources without the `asset:` prefix behave as before.
   - `Include/RmlUi/Core/AssetTexture.h` (new, included by `Include/RmlUi/Core.h`): `IsAssetTextureSource`, `SetAssetTextureRequester` installs the host function called on the RmlUi thread with the path after the prefix and an `AssetTextureRequest` (entry index and generation); `InstallAssetTexture` / `FailAssetTexture` install the size and an opaque host token, or a failure, into the render manager of a render interface. `Rml::Shutdown` clears the requester (`Source/Core/Core.cpp`).
   - `Source/Core/RenderManager.cpp` (`LoadTexture`): an `asset:` source skips `JoinPath`, like a `?` source, so `<img src>`, image decorators, `fill-image` and sprite sheets accept it.
   - `Source/Core/TextureDatabase.{h,cpp}` (`FileTextureDatabase`): an `asset:` source is an entry of the file database with the same states. Its first request calls the requester instead of launching a decode job (no requester: the entry fails and logs `Could not load texture`). `InstallAsset` applies the host's install only to a pending asset entry of the same generation; a failure, a zero size or a zero token marks it failed and logs `Could not load texture` once. `GetHandle` on a ready asset entry calls `RenderInterface::GenerateAssetTexture` with the token instead of `GenerateTexture`. Release paths are the file entry's (the token is cleared with the handle).
   - `Include/RmlUi/Core/RenderInterface.h`, `Source/Core/RenderInterface.cpp`: new virtual `GenerateAssetTexture(token, dimensions)`, returning 0 by default.
   - `Include/RmlUi/Core/RenderManager.h`, `Source/Core/RenderManager.cpp`, `Source/Core/RenderManagerAccess.{h,cpp}`: private `InstallAssetTexture`, reached by the free install functions.
   - ArcRmlUI: the requester pushes the request on the active view's outbound channel; `SArcRmlViewport` hands it to `FArcRmlAssetTextureRegistry` (`Host/`), which loads the texture with `FStreamableManager` on the game thread, holds it per view until the render thread has released the view, and installs the result through an `InstallAssetTexture` command. `FArcRmlRecordingRenderInterface::GenerateAssetTexture` records a texture resource that holds the texture's `FTextureReference`; the replay resolves its RHI texture on every draw and `TexturePS` premultiplies it, converting sRGB textures back to sRGB-encoded values first.
67. A compiled document's body can be instanced under an element of another document (ArcRmlUI tab menu embed plan step 1). Documents loaded with `LoadDocumentCompiled` are unchanged.
   - `Include/RmlUi/Core/Factory.h`, `Source/Core/Factory.cpp`: `InstanceDocumentCompiledBody(Element* parent, const CompiledDocument&, const String& source_url, SharedPtr<StyleSheetContainer>& out_style_sheet)` creates a `div` with the attributes of the document's `<body>` (`data-model`, `class`, …), appends it to `parent`, then replays the body's children into it, and returns it. The `div` is attached before its children are created, so every element gets its parent with the context present and a nested `data-model` looks up its own model (`Element::SetParent`). `out_style_sheet` is the head's style sheets combined as the document would combine them at load, or null when the head has none. The head creates no elements; its title and scripts are ignored. A `parent` outside a context, a document without `<body>`, or a failed instancer logs an error and returns null with no element added. The caller sets the sheet on the owner document (`ElementDocument::SetStyleSheetContainer`) and removes the `div` to undo the embed.
   - `Source/Core/XMLEventStream.{h,cpp}`: `XMLEventReplay::ReplayDocumentBody` replays the `<head>` events into an `XMLParser` without a root element, so `XMLNodeHandlerHead` fills a `DocumentHeader` and does not call `ProcessHeader` on any document, and replays the `<body>` events into an `XMLParser` rooted at the new `div`, where `XMLNodeHandlerBody` sets no attributes because the `div` is not a document. `Replay` is now `ReplayEvents` over the whole stream.
   - `Source/Core/DocumentHeader.{h,cpp}`: `MergeDocumentHeaderTemplates` (template merge, then the document's header) and `LoadDocumentHeaderStyleSheet` (inline sheets parsed, `<link>` sheets from `StyleSheetFactory`, combined in order) are moved out of `ElementDocument::ProcessHeader` (`Source/Core/ElementDocument.cpp`), which now calls them.
   - `Include/RmlUi/Core/Context.h`, `Source/Core/Context.cpp`: `Context::EmbedDocumentCompiled(Element* parent, const CompiledDocument&, const String& source_url, SharedPtr<StyleSheetContainer>& out_style_sheet)` is the entry hosts call (ArcRmlUI tab menu embed plan step 2). It seeds the data expression memo from the compiled table, calls `Factory::InstanceDocumentCompiledBody`, then updates the context's data models with the memo still alive, as `LoadDocumentCompiled` does. A `parent` from another context logs an error and returns null. `Factory::InstanceDocumentCompiledBody` no longer seeds a memo of its own.
